```


Conversion rises steeply with prior-year giving. Donors who gave more than $500 in FY t convert at `{python} pct(pb["over $500"]["rate"])` and supply `{python} pct(pb["over $500"]["share_of_converters"])` of converters while making up `{python} pct(pb["over $500"]["share_of_donors"], 2)` of eligible donor-years. Donors who gave $240 or less are `{python} pct(low_bands["share_of_donors"])` of donor-years and supply only `{python} pct(low_bands["share_of_converters"])` of converters. The pattern holds for never-major donors, whose top-band rate is `{python} pct(pb["over $500"]["never_major_rate"])`. Distance to $1,200 ranks donors in exactly the same order as prior-year giving, so it is not treated as a separate feature.

These five bands are the bands used for every comparison in the rest of this section.

### Features at the Prediction Date

The shared build adds the following features for each eligible donor at the end of FY t. The three-year total suggested in the individual EDAs is split into prior-year giving and giving in the two years before, since prior-year giving is already held constant by the bands.

| Feature | Definition |
|---|---|
| Former major donor | Major in any earlier fiscal year, including legacy years |
| Years given, last 5 | Fiscal years with a gift from FY t-4 to FY t |
| Years since first gift | Years from the first fiscal year with a gift, including legacy years, to FY t |
| Legacy-era giving years | Fiscal years with a legacy gift, Erin's legacy history indicator |
| Change from last year | FY t giving compared with FY t-1 giving |
| Giving in the two years before | Total giving in FY t-2 and FY t-1 |
| Largest gift share of FY t | Largest single gift as a share of FY t giving |
| Largest gift in FY t | Largest single gift in FY t |
| Upgrade or additional gift in FY t | A Unite payment in FY t with that gift type |
| Soft credit before FY t, in FY t | At least one soft credit in an earlier year, or in FY t |
| Monthly sustainer amount | Recurring payments in FY t divided by their number |
| Days since last gift | Days from the last gift to June 30 of FY t |

: Giving-history features built for each donor-year

### Signals Within Giving Bands

Following decision 7, a feature adds signal only if it separates converters among donors who gave about the same amount. For each level of a feature, we count how many converters we would expect if those donors converted at the average rate of their prior-year band, and divide the observed converters by that number. A ratio above 1 means the level converts more often than its prior-year giving predicts. A ratio near 1 means the feature's overall lift is prior-year giving in another form. Intervals come from the couple-clustered bootstrap used for the base rates. The same ratio is computed for never-major donors using their own band rates. The overall lift, the level's rate divided by the base rate of `{python} pct(base12, 3)`, is shown for context.

```{python}
#| label: within-band-signals

def yes_no(col):
    return pl.when(pl.col(col)).then(pl.lit("yes")).otherwise(pl.lit("no"))

# (feature, level expression, levels in display order)
signal_specs = [
    ("Former major donor", yes_no("former_major"), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Years given, last 5", pl.col("years_last5").cast(pl.String) + " of 5", ["1 of 5", "2 of 5", "3 of 5", "4 of 5", "5 of 5"]),
    ("Years since first gift", pl.col("years_since_first_gift").cut([1, 3, 10], labels=["1", "2 to 3", "4 to 10", "over 10"]).cast(pl.String),
     ["1", "2 to 3", "4 to 10", "over 10"]),
    ("Legacy-era giving years", pl.when(pl.col("legacy_years") == 0).then(pl.lit("none"))
        .when(pl.col("legacy_years") <= 4).then(pl.lit("1 to 4")).otherwise(pl.lit("5 or more")), ["none", "1 to 4", "5 or more"]),
    ("Change from last year", pl.when(pl.col("prev_total") == 0).then(pl.lit("no gift last year"))
        .when(pl.col("prior_total") > pl.col("prev_total")).then(pl.lit("gave more"))
        .when(pl.col("prior_total") < pl.col("prev_total")).then(pl.lit("gave less")).otherwise(pl.lit("gave the same")),
     ["no gift last year", "gave less", "gave the same", "gave more"]),
    ("Giving in the two years before", pl.when(pl.col("two_years_before") == 0).then(pl.lit("$0"))
        .when(pl.col("two_years_before") <= 500).then(pl.lit("$1 to $500"))
        .when(pl.col("two_years_before") < 1200).then(pl.lit("$501 to $1,199")).otherwise(pl.lit("$1,200 or more")),
     ["$0", "$1 to $500", "$501 to $1,199", "$1,200 or more"]),
    ("Largest gift share of FY t", pl.when(pl.col("largest_gift_t") >= pl.col("prior_total")).then(pl.lit("all in one gift"))
        .when(pl.col("largest_gift_t") >= 0.5 * pl.col("prior_total")).then(pl.lit("half or more")).otherwise(pl.lit("under half")),
     ["under half", "half or more", "all in one gift"]),
    ("Largest gift in FY t", pl.col("largest_gift_t").cut([100, 250, 500], labels=["$100 or less", "$101 to $250", "$251 to $500", "over $500"]).cast(pl.String),
     ["$100 or less", "$101 to $250", "$251 to $500", "over $500"]),
    ("Upgrade gift in FY t", yes_no("upgrade_gift"), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Additional gift in FY t", yes_no("additional_gift"), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Soft credit before FY t", yes_no("soft_before"), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Soft credit in FY t", yes_no("soft_in_t"), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Monthly sustainer amount", pl.when(~pl.col("sustainer")).then(pl.lit("not a sustainer"))
        .when(pl.col("monthly_amount") <= 10).then(pl.lit("$10 or less"))
        .when(pl.col("monthly_amount") <= 25).then(pl.lit("$11 to $25")).otherwise(pl.lit("over $25")),
     ["not a sustainer", "$10 or less", "$11 to $25", "over $25"]),
    ("Days since last gift", pl.col("days_since_last_gift").cut([30, 90, 180], labels=["30 or less", "31 to 90", "91 to 180", "over 180"]).cast(pl.String),
     ["30 or less", "31 to 90", "91 to 180", "over 180"]),
]

def couple_draws(df, reps=1000, seed=20261009):
    # each bootstrap draw counts how many times every couple is picked
    couples = df["couple_id"].unique().sort()
    idx = couples.search_sorted(df["couple_id"]).to_numpy()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    m = len(couples)
    w = np.stack([np.bincount(rng.integers(0, m, m), minlength=m) for _ in range(reps)]).astype(np.float32)
    return idx, w

def within_band_ratio(df, idx, w, levels):
    # observed converters over the number expected from each level's mix of prior-year bands
    nb, nl = len(PRIOR_BANDS), len(levels)
    level_i = df["level"].replace_strict({lev: i for i, lev in enumerate(levels)}, return_dtype=pl.Int64).to_numpy()
    cell = df["band"].to_physical().to_numpy() * nl + level_i
    rows = np.zeros((w.shape[1], nb * nl), np.float32)
    conv = np.zeros_like(rows)
    np.add.at(rows, (idx, cell), 1)
    np.add.at(conv, (idx, cell), df["converted"].to_numpy())

    def ratio(r, c):
        r, c = r.reshape(*r.shape[:-1], nb, nl), c.reshape(*c.shape[:-1], nb, nl)
        band_rate = c.sum(-1, keepdims=True) / np.maximum(r.sum(-1, keepdims=True), 1)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            return c.sum(-2) / (r * band_rate).sum(-2), (r * band_rate).sum(-2)

    est, expected = ratio(rows.sum(0), conv.sum(0))
    draws = np.vstack([ratio(w[s:s + 100] @ rows, w[s:s + 100] @ conv)[0] for s in range(0, len(w), 100)])
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
        lo, hi = np.nanquantile(draws, [0.025, 0.975], axis=0)
    return est, lo, hi, expected

def signal_table(feat, specs=signal_specs):
    # one row per feature level, for all eligible donors and for never-major donors
    idx, w = couple_draws(feat)
    never = ~feat["former_major"].to_numpy()
    base = feat["converted"].mean()
    out = []
    for name, expr, levels in specs:
        d = feat.with_columns(level=expr)
        est, lo, hi, expected = within_band_ratio(d, idx, w, levels)
        n_est, n_lo, n_hi, _ = within_band_ratio(d.filter(~pl.col("former_major")), idx[never], w, levels)
        counts = {r["level"]: r for r in d.group_by("level").agg(n=pl.len(), c=pl.col("converted").sum()).iter_rows(named=True)}
        for i, lev in enumerate(levels):
            n_rows, n_conv = counts[lev]["n"], counts[lev]["c"]
            out.append({"feature": name, "level": lev, "donor_years": n_rows, "converters": n_conv,
                        "rate": n_conv / n_rows, "lift": n_conv / n_rows / base, "expected": expected[i],
                        "ratio": est[i], "ci_low": lo[i], "ci_high": hi[i],
                        "never_ratio": None if name == "Former major donor" else n_est[i],
                        "never_low": None if name == "Former major donor" else n_lo[i],
                        "never_high": None if name == "Former major donor" else n_hi[i]})
    return pl.DataFrame(out)

def ratio_text(r, lo, hi, conv):
    if r is None:
        return "not applicable"
    return "no converters" if conv == 0 else f"{r:.2f} ({lo:.2f} to {hi:.2f})"

def display_signals(tbl):
    return tbl.with_columns(
        pl.col("lift").round(2), pl.col("expected").round(1),
        within_band_ratio=pl.struct("ratio", "ci_low", "ci_high", "converters").map_elements(
            lambda s: ratio_text(s["ratio"], s["ci_low"], s["ci_high"], s["converters"]), return_dtype=pl.String),
        never_major_ratio=pl.struct("never_ratio", "never_low", "never_high", "converters").map_elements(
            lambda s: ratio_text(s["never_ratio"], s["never_low"], s["never_high"], s["converters"]), return_dtype=pl.String),
    ).select("feature", "level", "donor_years", "converters", "rate", "lift", "expected", "within_band_ratio", "never_major_ratio")

signals12 = signal_table(feat12)

def sig(feature, level, col="ratio", tbl=signals12):
    return tbl.filter((pl.col("feature") == feature) & (pl.col("level") == level))[col][0]

def ci(feature, level, never=False, tbl=signals12):
    # a ratio with its interval, for the text
    cols = ("never_ratio", "never_low", "never_high") if never else ("ratio", "ci_low", "ci_high")
    r, lo, hi = (sig(feature, level, c, tbl) for c in cols)
    return f"{r:.2f} ({lo:.2f} to {hi:.2f})"

# share of converters at a level who are former major donors
def former_share(expr):
    return feat12.filter(expr & pl.col("converted"))["former_major"].mean()

former_gave_less = former_share(pl.col("prior_total") < pl.col("prev_total"))
former_two_years = former_share(pl.col("two_years_before") >= 1200)
former_soft_before = former_share(pl.col("soft_before"))

# where upgrade and soft-credit donors sit in prior-year giving
upgrade_top = (feat12.filter("upgrade_gift")["prior_total"] > 240).mean()
soft_t_top = (feat12.filter("soft_in_t")["prior_total"] > 240).mean()
all_top = (feat12["prior_total"] > 240).mean()

show(display_signals(signals12), pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="Giving-history signals: overall lift and ratio within prior-year bands, 12 month outcome")
```

```{python}
#| label: within-band-plot
#| fig-height: 11

plot_df = pl.concat([
    signals12.select("feature", "level", "ratio", "ci_low", "ci_high", "converters", group=pl.lit("All eligible")),
    signals12.select("feature", "level", ratio="never_ratio", ci_low="never_low", ci_high="never_high",
                     converters="converters", group=pl.lit("Never major")),
]).filter((pl.col("converters") > 0) & pl.col("ratio").is_not_null()).with_columns(
    # escape dollar signs so matplotlib does not read them as math
    label=(pl.col("feature") + ": " + pl.col("level")).str.replace_all("$", r"\$", literal=True)
)
label_order = list(dict.fromkeys(plot_df["label"].to_list()))[::-1]
plot_pd = plot_df.to_pandas()
plot_pd["label"] = plot_pd["label"].astype("category").cat.set_categories(label_order)

(
    ggplot(plot_pd, aes("label", "ratio", color="group"))
    + geom_hline(yintercept=1, linetype="dashed", color="grey")
    + geom_pointrange(aes(ymin="ci_low", ymax="ci_high"), position=position_dodge(width=0.6), size=0.3)
    + scale_y_log10()
    + coord_flip()
    + labs(x="", y="Observed over expected converters (log scale)", color="",
           title="Signal beyond prior-year giving",
           subtitle="12 month outcome, FY2021 to FY2024 cohorts, 95% intervals")
    + theme(figure_size=(8, 11), legend_position="top")
)
```

Most features with large overall lift add much less once prior-year giving is held constant:

- **Former major status is one of the largest added signals.** Former major donors convert at `{python} ci("Former major donor", "yes")` times the rate their prior-year giving predicts. Only giving less than the year before is higher, and those converters are mostly former major donors as well (below).
- **Short giving histories are the clearest negative signal.** Donors in their first year of giving, donors who gave in only one of the last five years, and donors with no gift the year before convert at about a fifth of the expected rate (`{python} f'{sig("Years since first gift", "1"):.2f}'`, `{python} f'{sig("Years given, last 5", "1 of 5"):.2f}'`, and `{python} f'{sig("Change from last year", "no gift last year"):.2f}'`). This holds for never-major donors (`{python} f'{sig("Years since first gift", "1", "never_ratio"):.2f}'`, `{python} f'{sig("Years given, last 5", "1 of 5", "never_ratio"):.2f}'`, and `{python} f'{sig("Change from last year", "no gift last year", "never_ratio"):.2f}'`). The gain at the other end is smaller: giving in all five years is `{python} ci("Years given, last 5", "5 of 5")` overall and `{python} ci("Years given, last 5", "5 of 5", never=True)` for never-major donors.
- **Legacy history helps.** Donors with no legacy-era gifts convert at `{python} ci("Legacy-era giving years", "none")` times the expected rate, and `{python} ci("Legacy-era giving years", "none", never=True)` among never-major donors. This supports keeping Erin's legacy history indicators alongside the legacy amounts.
- **Some signals mostly mark former major donors.** Giving less than the year before, $1,200 or more in the two years before, and a soft credit before FY t have ratios of `{python} ci("Change from last year", "gave less")`, `{python} ci("Giving in the two years before", "$1,200 or more")`, and `{python} ci("Soft credit before FY t", "yes")`. Among never-major donors they fall to `{python} ci("Change from last year", "gave less", never=True)`, `{python} ci("Giving in the two years before", "$1,200 or more", never=True)`, and `{python} ci("Soft credit before FY t", "yes", never=True)`, with intervals that include 1. The converters at these levels are mostly former major donors stepping down from a major year (`{python} pct(former_gave_less, 0)`, `{python} pct(former_two_years, 0)`, and `{python} pct(former_soft_before, 0)`).
- **Upgrade gifts and soft credits in FY t add nothing.** An upgrade gift has an overall lift of `{python} f'{sig("Upgrade gift in FY t", "yes", "lift"):.1f}'` and a soft credit in FY t `{python} f'{sig("Soft credit in FY t", "yes", "lift"):.1f}'`, and Benjamin's and Kate's EDAs listed both as strong signals on that basis. Within bands the ratios are `{python} ci("Upgrade gift in FY t", "yes")` and `{python} ci("Soft credit in FY t", "yes")`, and for never-major donors `{python} ci("Upgrade gift in FY t", "yes", never=True)` and `{python} ci("Soft credit in FY t", "yes", never=True)`. Their overall lift comes from where these donors sit: `{python} "all" if upgrade_top == 1 else pct(upgrade_top, 0) + " of"` upgrade-gift donor-years and `{python} pct(soft_t_top, 0)` of soft-credit donor-years gave more than $240 in FY t, compared with `{python} pct(all_top)` of all eligible donor-years.
- **How the year's giving was made matters a little.** Donors who gave the year's whole amount in one gift convert at `{python} ci("Largest gift share of FY t", "all in one gift")` times the expected rate (`{python} ci("Largest gift share of FY t", "all in one gift", never=True)` for never-major donors). Additional gifts point the other way, at `{python} ci("Additional gift in FY t", "yes", never=True)` among never-major donors.
- **Sustainers convert somewhat less than their giving predicts.** Sustainers giving $10 a month or less are at `{python} ci("Monthly sustainer amount", "$10 or less")`, and none of the `{python} n(sig("Monthly sustainer amount", "over $25", "donor_years"))` donor-years giving more than $25 a month converted, where about `{python} f'{sig("Monthly sustainer amount", "over $25", "expected"):.0f}'` were expected.

### Recency and Sustainer Status

Overall, recency looks like a strong signal: donors whose last gift came within 30 days of year end have a lift of `{python} f'{sig("Days since last gift", "30 or less", "lift"):.1f}'`, while the 31 to 90 day group has a lift of `{python} f'{sig("Days since last gift", "31 to 90", "lift"):.2f}'`. Within bands the order changes: the most recent group falls to `{python} f'{sig("Days since last gift", "30 or less"):.2f}'`, and donors whose last gift was more than 180 days before year end are highest at `{python} f'{sig("Days since last gift", "over 180"):.2f}'`. Monthly sustainers drive much of the overall pattern, so the table splits recency by sustainer status.

```{python}
#| label: recency-sustainer

sust_recency = feat12.with_columns(
    level=pl.when(pl.col("sustainer"))
        .then(pl.lit("sustainer, ") + pl.col("days_since_last_gift").cut([30, 90], labels=["30 or less", "31 to 90", "over 90"]).cast(pl.String))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("not a sustainer, ") + pl.col("days_since_last_gift").cut([30, 90, 180], labels=["30 or less", "31 to 90", "91 to 180", "over 180"]).cast(pl.String))
)
rs_levels = ["sustainer, 30 or less", "sustainer, 31 to 90", "sustainer, over 90",
             "not a sustainer, 30 or less", "not a sustainer, 31 to 90", "not a sustainer, 91 to 180", "not a sustainer, over 180"]
rs_idx, rs_w = couple_draws(sust_recency)
rs_est, rs_lo, rs_hi, rs_exp = within_band_ratio(sust_recency, rs_idx, rs_w, rs_levels)
rs_counts = {r["level"]: r for r in sust_recency.group_by("level").agg(n=pl.len(), c=pl.col("converted").sum()).iter_rows(named=True)}
recency_sustainer = pl.DataFrame([
    {"group": lev, "donor_years": rs_counts[lev]["n"], "converters": rs_counts[lev]["c"],
     "rate": rs_counts[lev]["c"] / rs_counts[lev]["n"], "expected": round(float(rs_exp[i]), 1),
     "within_band_ratio": ratio_text(rs_est[i], rs_lo[i], rs_hi[i], rs_counts[lev]["c"])}
    for i, lev in enumerate(rs_levels)
])
rs = {r["group"]: r for r in recency_sustainer.iter_rows(named=True)}
sust_share_31_90 = feat12.filter(pl.col("days_since_last_gift").is_between(31, 90))["sustainer"].mean()

# share of sustainers above $240 in FY t, by recency
sust = feat12.filter("sustainer")
sust_top_recent = (sust.filter(pl.col("days_since_last_gift") <= 30)["prior_total"] > 240).mean()
sust_top_31_90 = (sust.filter(pl.col("days_since_last_gift").is_between(31, 90))["prior_total"] > 240).mean()

show(recency_sustainer, pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="Recency split by sustainer status, within prior-year bands")
```

Sustainers make up `{python} pct(sust_share_31_90)` of the 31 to 90 day group. In raw rates, sustainers with a gift in the last 30 days convert at `{python} pct(rs["sustainer, 30 or less"]["rate"], 2)` and those whose last gift was 31 to 90 days before year end at `{python} pct(rs["sustainer, 31 to 90"]["rate"], 3)`. That gap comes from prior-year giving, not recency: `{python} pct(sust_top_recent, 0)` of the recent sustainers gave more than $240 in FY t, compared with `{python} pct(sust_top_31_90)` of the others. Within bands both groups convert below their expected rate (`{python} rs["sustainer, 30 or less"]["within_band_ratio"]` and `{python} rs["sustainer, 31 to 90"]["within_band_ratio"]`). Among donors who are not sustainers, the most recent and least recent groups are both above expected (`{python} rs["not a sustainer, 30 or less"]["within_band_ratio"]` and `{python} rs["not a sustainer, over 180"]["within_band_ratio"]`) and the middle groups are near 1, so there is no steady trend. Sustainer status carries more information than recency, and recency should not be scored as a straight line. This matters for the recency, frequency, and value baseline in the baselines section.

### Longer Window Check

The same comparison for the 3 year outcome uses the FY2021 and FY2022 cohorts, the only ones whose 3 year windows end before FY2026.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Signals within giving bands, 3 year outcome

```{python}
#| label: within-band-3yr

signals3 = signal_table(feat3)
show(display_signals(signals3), pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="Giving-history signals within prior-year bands, 3 year outcome")
```
:::

```{python}
#| label: within-band-compare

# levels with at least 10 converters at 12 months, and whether the 3 year ratio falls on the same side of 1
both = signals12.join(signals3.select("feature", "level", ratio3="ratio", conv3="converters"), on=["feature", "level"]).filter(
    (pl.col("converters") >= 10) & (pl.col("conv3") >= 10)
)
same_side = ((both["ratio"] > 1) == (both["ratio3"] > 1)).mean()
flipped = both.filter((pl.col("ratio") > 1) != (pl.col("ratio3") > 1))
flipped_low = flipped.select(pl.min_horizontal("ratio", "ratio3")).to_series().min()
flipped_high = flipped.select(pl.max_horizontal("ratio", "ratio3")).to_series().max()
```

The 3 year results follow the 12 month results closely: for the `{python} n(both.height)` levels with at least 10 converters in both windows, `{python} pct(same_side, 0)` of the ratios fall on the same side of 1. The `{python} n(flipped.height)` levels that switch sides all have ratios between `{python} f"{flipped_low:.2f}"` and `{python} f"{flipped_high:.2f}"` in both windows, so none of them changes from a clear signal to its opposite. Former major status and short giving histories remain the strongest signals at 3 years.

### Summary for Modeling

- Prior-year giving carries most of the signal. The other features should be judged by what they add to it, and most add much less than their overall lift suggests.
- The features that add signal are former major status, giving history length (years given in the last five, years since first gift, legacy-era years, a gift the year before), whether the year's giving came in one gift, and sustainer status. Recency adds little once prior-year giving and sustainer status are known.
- Upgrade gifts and soft credits in FY t can stay in the feature set, but they should not be described to staff as signs of major potential.
- Among never-major donors, the added signal is mostly about history length and the shape of the year's giving, so the model will rely heavily on prior-year giving for this group.

## Solicitation and Passport Viewing

The individual EDAs disagreed on whether solicitation and Passport viewing help predict conversion. Erin's and Samantha's EDAs compared overall rates, while Benjamin's and Kate's compared rates within bands of prior-year giving. This section applies the within-band test from the previous section (decision 7) to both, using the same validation cohorts, the 12 month outcome, and the same five bands. Both sources only begin in FY2021, so they cannot be used for cohorts before then.

### Solicitation Volume and Timing

```{python}
#| label: solicitation-volume

sol = bp.solicitation_by_year(clean)
cm_dates = clean["campaign_members"]
start_marker = cm_dates["campaign_start_date"].dt.strftime("%m-%d").unique().to_list()
responses = cm_dates.filter("responded").with_columns(
    campaign_fy=bp.fiscal_year("campaign_start_date"), response_fy=bp.fiscal_year("responded_date"))
response_same_fy = (responses["campaign_fy"] == responses["response_fy"]).mean()
response_types = responses["response_type"].unique().to_list()

donors_fy = person_years.select("constituent_id", "fy")
sol_volume = (
    sol.join(donors_fy, on=["constituent_id", "fy"], how="semi")
    .group_by("fy")
    .agg(donors_solicited=pl.len(), solicitations=pl.col("solicitations").sum(), responses=pl.col("responses").sum())
    .join(donors_fy.group_by("fy").agg(donors=pl.len()), on="fy")
    .with_columns(share_of_donors_solicited=pl.col("donors_solicited") / pl.col("donors"),
                  solicitations_per_donor=(pl.col("solicitations") / pl.col("donors_solicited")).round(1),
                  response_rate=pl.col("responses") / pl.col("solicitations"))
    .select("fy", "donors", "share_of_donors_solicited", "solicitations_per_donor", "response_rate")
    .sort("fy")
)
sv = {r["fy"]: r for r in sol_volume.iter_rows(named=True)}
show(sol_volume, pct_cols=["share_of_donors_solicited", "response_rate"], caption="Share of donors solicited and response rate by fiscal year")
```

Every campaign start date is `{python} start_marker[0].replace("-", "/") if len(start_marker) == 1 else "varied"`, so it marks the fiscal year and not the date of the ask. A response is a payment on that marketing code (the only response type is `{python} response_types[0]`). Following Samantha's rule, a response counts in the fiscal year of its response date, since that is when it becomes known. In this data `{python} "every response falls" if response_same_fy == 1 else pct(response_same_fy) + " of responses fall"` in the same fiscal year as its campaign, so the rule gives the same counts as using the campaign year, and every response used for a FY t snapshot is known by June 30 of FY t.

The share of donors solicited rose from `{python} pct(sv[2021]["share_of_donors_solicited"])` in FY2021 to `{python} pct(sv[2022]["share_of_donors_solicited"])` in FY2022 and nearly all donors from FY2023 on, while solicitations per solicited donor stayed close to `{python} f'{sol_volume["solicitations_per_donor"].median():.0f}'`. That change reflects PBS Utah's mailing decisions, not donor behavior, so whether a donor was solicited depends partly on the year.

### Solicitation Within Giving Bands

Solicitation features are counted for FY t: number of solicitations, responses, and whether any solicitation came by mail, email, digital, or phone and in person combined (both are rare). The three-year count follows Erin's EDA and covers FY t-2 to FY t. Because solicitation records start in FY2021, the FY2021 and FY2022 cohorts have only one and two years of it.

```{python}
#| label: solicitation-signals

feat_sol = feat12.join(bp.solicitation_features(feat12, sol), on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left")
share_solicited = (feat_sol["solicitations"] > 0).mean()
unsolicited_cohorts = sorted(feat_sol.filter(pl.col("solicitations") == 0)["t"].unique().to_list())

sol_specs = [
    ("Solicitations in FY t", pl.col("solicitations").cut([0, 1, 10, 30], labels=["none", "1", "2 to 10", "11 to 30", "over 30"]).cast(pl.String),
     ["none", "1", "2 to 10", "11 to 30", "over 30"]),
    ("Solicitations, FY t-2 to FY t", pl.col("solicitations_3yr").cut([0, 5, 20, 60], labels=["none", "1 to 5", "6 to 20", "21 to 60", "over 60"]).cast(pl.String),
     ["none", "1 to 5", "6 to 20", "21 to 60", "over 60"]),
    ("Responses in FY t", pl.col("responses").cut([0, 1], labels=["none", "1", "2 or more"]).cast(pl.String), ["none", "1", "2 or more"]),
    ("Mail solicitation in FY t", yes_no("by_mail"), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Email solicitation in FY t", yes_no("by_email"), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Digital solicitation in FY t", yes_no("by_digital"), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Phone or in-person solicitation in FY t", yes_no("by_phone_or_in_person"), ["no", "yes"]),
]
sol_signals = signal_table(feat_sol, sol_specs)

def ssig(feature, level, col="ratio"):
    return sig(feature, level, col, tbl=sol_signals)

def sci(feature, level, never=False):
    return ci(feature, level, never, tbl=sol_signals)

show(display_signals(sol_signals), pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="Solicitation features within prior-year bands, 12 month outcome")
```

`{python} pct(share_solicited)` of eligible donors were solicited at least once in FY t, and every unsolicited donor-year comes from the `{python} " and ".join(f"FY{t}" for t in unsolicited_cohorts)` `{python} "cohort" if len(unsolicited_cohorts) == 1 else "cohorts"`, before solicitation reached nearly everyone. Once prior-year giving is held constant, solicitation adds little:

- **Volume.** No volume group converts clearly more or less often than its giving predicts, and most intervals include 1. The highest volume groups are `{python} sci("Solicitations in FY t", "over 30")` in FY t and `{python} sci("Solicitations, FY t-2 to FY t", "over 60")` over three years.
- **Responses.** Donors with one response have an overall lift of `{python} f'{ssig("Responses in FY t", "1", "lift"):.2f}'` but a within-band ratio of `{python} sci("Responses in FY t", "1")`. A response is a payment that is already part of prior-year giving, so it carries little new information.
- **Channels.** No channel stands out. Phone or in-person solicitation, which might mark donors staff already see as prospects, reaches `{python} n(ssig("Phone or in-person solicitation in FY t", "yes", "donor_years"))` donor-years and only `{python} n(ssig("Phone or in-person solicitation in FY t", "yes", "converters"))` converters, a ratio of `{python} sci("Phone or in-person solicitation in FY t", "yes")`.

### Solicitations in the Outcome Year

```{python}
#| label: outcome-year-solicitations

next_sol = sol.select("constituent_id", t=pl.col("fy") - 1, outcome_year=pl.col("solicitations"))
outcome_sol = (
    feat_sol.join(next_sol, on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left")
    .with_columns(pl.col("outcome_year").fill_null(0), top_band=pl.col("band") == "over $500")
    .group_by("top_band", "converted")
    .agg(donor_years=pl.len(), solicitations_fy_t=pl.col("solicitations").mean(), solicitations_outcome_year=pl.col("outcome_year").mean())
    .with_columns(pl.col("solicitations_fy_t", "solicitations_outcome_year").round(1),
                  group=pl.when(pl.col("top_band")).then(pl.lit("gave over $500 in FY t")).otherwise(pl.lit("gave $500 or less")))
    .select("group", "converted", "donor_years", "solicitations_fy_t", "solicitations_outcome_year")
    .sort("group", "converted")
)
osol = {(r["group"], r["converted"]): r for r in outcome_sol.iter_rows(named=True)}
top = "gave over $500 in FY t"
show(outcome_sol, caption="Average solicitations in FY t and in the outcome year, converters compared with others")
```

Among donors who gave over $500 in FY t, converters and non-converters received a similar number of solicitations in FY t (`{python} osol[(top, True)]["solicitations_fy_t"]` and `{python} osol[(top, False)]["solicitations_fy_t"]` on average). In the outcome year, converters received `{python} osol[(top, True)]["solicitations_outcome_year"]` and non-converters `{python} osol[(top, False)]["solicitations_outcome_year"]`. The data does not say why, but outcome-year solicitations move with the outcome and must not be used as features. Outcome-year responses are payments in the outcome year and are excluded for the same reason.

### Passport Coverage

The Passport table records titles viewed and the average share of each title watched, by person, fiscal year, and genre. A person-year only appears if something was watched, so a missing year can mean no linked account, no consent to share viewing, or no viewing. Following Erin's EDA, a missing year is kept as its own "no viewing record" level instead of being treated as zero viewing.

```{python}
#| label: passport-coverage

pv = clean["passport"]
viewer_years = pv.select("constituent_id", fy=pl.col("fiscal_year")).unique()

def again_next_year(df, fy):
    this_year = df.filter(pl.col("fy") == fy)
    return this_year.join(df.filter(pl.col("fy") == fy + 1), on="constituent_id", how="semi").height / this_year.height

passport_cov = pl.DataFrame([
    {"fy": fy, "viewers": viewer_years.filter(pl.col("fy") == fy).height,
     "share_who_gave": viewer_years.filter(pl.col("fy") == fy).join(donors_fy, on=["constituent_id", "fy"], how="semi").height
                       / viewer_years.filter(pl.col("fy") == fy).height,
     "viewers_again_next_year": again_next_year(viewer_years, fy), "donors_again_next_year": again_next_year(donors_fy, fy)}
    for fy in range(2021, 2026)
])
view_again = passport_cov["viewers_again_next_year"]
give_again = passport_cov["donors_again_next_year"]
show(passport_cov, pct_cols=["share_who_gave", "viewers_again_next_year", "donors_again_next_year"], caption="Passport viewers by year and how often viewing carries over")
```

Most viewers gave in the same year, which fits Passport being a member benefit. Viewing carries over from year to year much less than giving does: `{python} pct(view_again.min(), 0)` to `{python} pct(view_again.max(), 0)` of a year's viewers have a record the next year, compared with `{python} pct(give_again.min(), 0)` to `{python} pct(give_again.max(), 0)` of donors who give again. This affects how viewing features behave, because a donor's viewing record in FY t says little about the next year, so the analysis includes both a FY t flag and a flag for any viewing record through FY t.

### Passport Within Giving Bands

```{python}
#| label: passport-signals

feat_pv = feat12.join(bp.passport_features(feat12, pv), on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left")
share_viewed_t = feat_pv["viewed_t"].mean()
rho_titles_prior = feat_pv.filter("viewed_t").select(pl.corr("titles", "prior_total", method="spearman")).item()

NO_RECORD = "no viewing record"
def viewing_level(expr, cuts, labels):
    return pl.when(~pl.col("viewed_t")).then(pl.lit(NO_RECORD)).otherwise(expr.cut(cuts, labels=labels).cast(pl.String))

pv_specs = [
    ("Viewing record in FY t", yes_no("viewed_t"), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Viewing record through FY t", yes_no("viewed_by_t"), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Titles viewed in FY t", viewing_level(pl.col("titles"), [15, 40], ["1 to 15", "16 to 40", "over 40"]),
     [NO_RECORD, "1 to 15", "16 to 40", "over 40"]),
    ("Genres viewed in FY t", viewing_level(pl.col("genres"), [2, 4], ["1 to 2", "3 to 4", "5 or more"]),
     [NO_RECORD, "1 to 2", "3 to 4", "5 or more"]),
    ("Share of titles watched", viewing_level(pl.col("share_watched"), [0.6, 0.85], ["under 60%", "60% to 85%", "over 85%"]),
     [NO_RECORD, "under 60%", "60% to 85%", "over 85%"]),
]
pv_signals = signal_table(feat_pv, pv_specs)

def psig(feature, level, col="ratio"):
    return sig(feature, level, col, tbl=pv_signals)

def pci(feature, level, never=False):
    return ci(feature, level, never, tbl=pv_signals)

# titles viewed, observed over expected in each cohort and at 3 years (band rates from the pooled cohorts)
def titles_by(feat, by):
    return (
        feat.with_columns(level=pv_specs[2][1], band_rate=pl.col("converted").mean().over("band"))
        .group_by(by).agg(observed=pl.col("converted").sum(), expected=pl.col("band_rate").sum())
        .with_columns(ratio=pl.col("observed") / pl.col("expected"))
    )

titles_cohort = titles_by(feat_pv, ["t", "level"])
heavy_by_cohort = titles_cohort.filter(pl.col("level") == "over 40")
light_by_cohort = titles_cohort.filter(pl.col("level") == "1 to 15")
feat_pv3 = feat3.join(bp.passport_features(feat3, pv), on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left")
titles3 = {r["level"]: r["ratio"] for r in titles_by(feat_pv3, ["level"]).iter_rows(named=True)}

show(display_signals(pv_signals), pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="Passport features within prior-year bands, 12 month outcome")
```

`{python} pct(share_viewed_t)` of eligible donors have a viewing record in FY t, and among them the rank correlation between titles viewed and prior-year giving is `{python} f"{rho_titles_prior:.2f}"`, so viewing and giving are nearly unrelated. Having a viewing record adds nothing: viewers have an overall lift of `{python} f'{psig("Viewing record in FY t", "yes", "lift"):.2f}'` and a within-band ratio of `{python} pci("Viewing record in FY t", "yes")`. Completion and genre breadth add little as well, with intervals that include 1 at every level.

The number of titles viewed is the exception. Light viewers (1 to 15 titles) convert at `{python} pci("Titles viewed in FY t", "1 to 15")` times their expected rate and heavy viewers (over 40 titles) at `{python} pci("Titles viewed in FY t", "over 40")`, or `{python} pci("Titles viewed in FY t", "over 40", never=True)` among never-major donors. The direction holds in each validation cohort, with heavy viewers between `{python} f'{heavy_by_cohort["ratio"].min():.2f}'` and `{python} f'{heavy_by_cohort["ratio"].max():.2f}'` and light viewers between `{python} f'{light_by_cohort["ratio"].min():.2f}'` and `{python} f'{light_by_cohort["ratio"].max():.2f}'`. However, each cohort has at most `{python} n(titles_cohort.filter(pl.col("level") != NO_RECORD)["observed"].max())` converters per group, and at 3 years the pattern mostly fades (`{python} f'{titles3["1 to 15"]:.2f}'` for light viewers and `{python} f'{titles3["over 40"]:.2f}'` for heavy viewers). Titles viewed is worth testing in the 12 month model, but it is a modest and uncertain signal.

### Summary for Modeling

- Solicitation adds no clear signal once prior-year giving is known. Responses are payments already counted in giving, and the solicitation counts partly reflect PBS Utah's mailing decisions.
- Having a Passport viewing record adds nothing either. The number of titles viewed shows a modest 12 month signal that should be tested in the model but not relied on.
- The overall differences that some individual EDAs found for both sources come mostly from giving level, which explains most of the disagreement among them.
- Outcome-year solicitations and responses must be excluded. Passport features should keep a "no viewing record" level, and viewing records rarely persist from year to year.
- Neither source reaches back before FY2021, so the 5 year outcome, which needs earlier cohorts, has to do without them. This costs little.

## Snapshot Fields and Leakage

The constituent table has one row per person, measured at the end of the data (FY2026). A field can only be a feature if its value at an earlier prediction date would have been the same, or if it can be rebuilt for that date. This section checks what each varying field encodes, tests the usable ones within giving bands, and collects the leakage rules from the whole notebook.

### PBS Classification Fields

```{python}
#| label: snapshot-classes

con = clean["constituents"]
people = con.filter(pl.col("primary_constituent_type") != "Organization")
fy26 = person_years.filter(pl.col("fy") == 2026)
status = (
    people.select("constituent_id", "major_donor_class_pbs_utah", "annual_giving_group", "sustainer_pbs_utah",
                  "lifetime_uofu_fundraising", "previous_fy_uofu_cash", "prospect_committed_giving_amount_uofu")
    .join(fy26.select("constituent_id", total_fy26="total", recurring_fy26="recurring_amt"), on="constituent_id", how="left")
    .join(person_years.filter(pl.col("fy") == 2025).select("constituent_id", total_fy25="total"), on="constituent_id", how="left")
    .join(person_years.group_by("constituent_id").agg(
              lifetime_pbs=pl.col("total").sum(),
              major_before_fy26=pl.col("major_individual").filter(pl.col("fy") < 2026).any()),
          on="constituent_id", how="left")
    .with_columns(pl.col("total_fy26", "recurring_fy26", "total_fy25", "lifetime_pbs").fill_null(0),
                  pl.col("major_before_fy26").fill_null(False))
)

class_decode = (
    status.group_by(major_donor_class=pl.col("major_donor_class_pbs_utah").fill_null("(blank)"))
    .agg(people=pl.len(), major_alone_in_fy26=(pl.col("total_fy26") >= 1200).mean(),
         major_before_fy26=pl.col("major_before_fy26").mean(),
         min_fy26_giving=pl.col("total_fy26").min(), max_fy26_giving=pl.col("total_fy26").max())
    .sort("people")
)
group_decode = (
    status.filter(pl.col("annual_giving_group").is_not_null())
    .group_by("annual_giving_group")
    .agg(people=pl.len(), gave_in_fy26=(pl.col("total_fy26") > 0).mean(),
         min_fy26_giving=pl.col("total_fy26").filter(pl.col("total_fy26") > 0).min(),
         max_fy26_giving=pl.col("total_fy26").max())
    .sort("min_fy26_giving", nulls_last=False)
)
cd = {r["major_donor_class"]: r for r in class_decode.iter_rows(named=True)}
sustainer_match = (status["sustainer_pbs_utah"] == (status["recurring_fy26"] > 0)).mean()

# how the snapshot classifies the couple that is major only in combination
couple_snapshot = (
    person_years.filter("major_combined_only")
    .join(con.select("constituent_id", "major_donor_class_pbs_utah", "annual_giving_group"), on="constituent_id")
)

show(class_decode, pct_cols=["major_alone_in_fy26", "major_before_fy26"], caption="Major donor class compared with FY2026 giving")
```

```{python}
#| label: snapshot-groups
show(group_decode, pct_cols=["gave_in_fy26"], caption="Annual giving group compared with FY2026 giving")
```

All three PBS classifications describe FY2026 giving:

- **Major donor class.** Broadcaster and Director are exactly the people who gave $1,200 or more on their own in FY2026, with Broadcasters at exactly $1,200 and Directors at $2,000 or more. Former means major in an earlier year but not in FY2026, and a blank means never major. The documented ranges ($1,000 to $4,999 for Broadcaster and $5,000 to $9,999 for Director) do not match the data.
- **Annual giving group.** Its meaning is listed as unknown, but it lines up with FY2026 giving: ND is no gift in FY2026, and PD, LD, SL, and CD are increasing ranges, with CD starting at $1,200.
- **Sustainer flag.** It matches "had recurring payments in FY2026" for `{python} pct(sustainer_match)` of people.

For any cohort before FY2025 these fields come from after the outcome year, and for the FY2025 cohort they are the outcome. All three are dropped. The earlier sections rebuild the same information for any year from the giving panel (former major status, monthly sustainer amount).

The snapshot also bears on the household rule. The `{python} n(couple_snapshot.height)` spouses who reach $1,200 only together in FY2026 have a `{python} "blank" if couple_snapshot["major_donor_class_pbs_utah"].is_null().all() else "non-blank"` major donor class, and each is in giving group `{python} ", ".join(sorted(set(couple_snapshot["annual_giving_group"].to_list())))` on their own giving. In this data, PBS's own classification counts major status per person without combining spouses. The team's rule came from PBS's description of how it counts households, so this is a point to confirm with PBS, although it affects only this one couple.

### University of Utah Fields

The problem statement lists University of Utah capacity information as an input. The three UofU dollar fields were compared with each person's PBS giving.

```{python}
#| label: uofu-fields

givers = status.filter(pl.col("lifetime_pbs") > 0)
cash_bands = (
    status.group_by("previous_fy_uofu_cash")
    .agg(people=pl.len(), min_fy25_giving=pl.col("total_fy25").min(), max_fy25_giving=pl.col("total_fy25").max())
    .sort("previous_fy_uofu_cash")
)
# do the FY2025 giving ranges of the cash codes overlap?
cash_ranges = cash_bands.filter(pl.col("previous_fy_uofu_cash") > 0).sort("min_fy25_giving")
cash_overlap = (cash_ranges["min_fy25_giving"].shift(-1) <= cash_ranges["max_fy25_giving"]).sum()

uofu_checks = pl.DataFrame([
    {"field": "Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "check": "correlation with lifetime PBS giving",
     "value": f'{givers.select(pl.corr("lifetime_uofu_fundraising", "lifetime_pbs")).item():.2f}'},
    {"field": "Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "check": "at least as large as lifetime PBS giving",
     "value": pct((givers["lifetime_uofu_fundraising"] >= givers["lifetime_pbs"]).mean())},
    {"field": "Previous FY UofU Cash", "check": "positive exactly when the person gave in FY2025",
     "value": pct(((status["previous_fy_uofu_cash"] > 0) == (status["total_fy25"] > 0)).mean())},
    {"field": "Previous FY UofU Cash", "check": "distinct values",
     "value": n(status["previous_fy_uofu_cash"].n_unique())},
    {"field": "Prospect Committed Giving UofU", "check": "positive exactly when the sustainer flag is set",
     "value": pct(((status["prospect_committed_giving_amount_uofu"] > 0) == status["sustainer_pbs_utah"]).mean())},
    {"field": "Prospect Committed Giving UofU", "check": "equal to FY2026 recurring giving",
     "value": pct((status["prospect_committed_giving_amount_uofu"] == status["recurring_fy26"]).mean())},
])
uc = {(r["field"], r["check"]): r["value"] for r in uofu_checks.iter_rows(named=True)}
show(uofu_checks, caption="How the UofU dollar fields relate to PBS giving")
```

```{python}
#| label: uofu-cash-bands
show(cash_bands, caption="Previous FY UofU Cash values and the FY2025 PBS giving behind each")
```

None of the three is independent of PBS giving:

- **Lifetime UofU Fundraising** has a correlation of `{python} uc[("Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "correlation with lifetime PBS giving")]` with lifetime PBS giving through FY2026 and is at least as large for `{python} uc[("Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "at least as large as lifetime PBS giving")]` of donors, so it looks like a total that includes PBS giving.
- **Previous FY UofU Cash** takes only `{python} uc[("Previous FY UofU Cash", "distinct values")]` values, and each one matches a range of the person's FY2025 PBS giving that `{python} "does not overlap" if cash_overlap == 0 else "partly overlaps"` the others. It is a coded version of FY2025 PBS giving.
- **Prospect Committed Giving** is positive exactly when the sustainer flag is set (`{python} uc[("Prospect Committed Giving UofU", "positive exactly when the sustainer flag is set")]` agreement) and equals FY2026 recurring giving for `{python} uc[("Prospect Committed Giving UofU", "equal to FY2026 recurring giving")]` of people.

```{python}
#| label: uofu-leak-strength

# how strong the lifetime field would look if it were used
feat_snap = feat12.join(
    con.select("constituent_id", "lifetime_uofu_fundraising", "age", "gender", "address_state",
               "primary_constituent_type", "spouse_constituent_id"),
    on="constituent_id", how="left",
)
leak_specs = [
    ("Lifetime UofU Fundraising", pl.col("lifetime_uofu_fundraising").cut([1000, 5000], labels=["$1,000 or less", "$1,001 to $5,000", "over $5,000"]).cast(pl.String),
     ["$1,000 or less", "$1,001 to $5,000", "over $5,000"]),
]
leak_signals = signal_table(feat_snap, leak_specs)
show(display_signals(leak_signals), pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="How strong lifetime UofU fundraising would look if used (it leaks the outcome)")
```

Used as a feature, the lifetime field would look as strong as former major status. Donors above $5,000 convert at `{python} pct(sig("Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "over $5,000", "rate", tbl=leak_signals))`, `{python} ci("Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "over $5,000", tbl=leak_signals)` times what their prior-year giving predicts, and `{python} ci("Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "over $5,000", never=True, tbl=leak_signals)` times among never-major donors, the largest ratio for that group in the notebook. That strength comes from counting the outcome years. All three UofU fields are dropped, which leaves no measure of giving capacity outside PBS Utah.

### Fields That Can Be Used

The remaining varying fields describe the person rather than their giving. Age is shifted back to the prediction date by subtracting the years between FY t and FY2026, assuming the snapshot age is as of FY2026. Gender, state, and having a spouse on file are assumed not to change. Constituent type is included here only as the sensitivity check the team agreed on, since it may be a label that changed over time.

```{python}
#| label: usable-snapshot

feat_snap = feat_snap.with_columns(
    age_at_t=pl.col("age") - (2026 - pl.col("t")),
    type_group=pl.when(pl.col("primary_constituent_type").is_in(["Friends", "Donors"])).then(pl.col("primary_constituent_type"))
        .when(pl.col("primary_constituent_type").str.starts_with("Alumni")).then(pl.lit("Alumni"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("other University affiliation")),
)
AGE_LABELS = ["40 or under", "41 to 55", "56 to 70", "71 to 85", "over 85"]
demo_specs = [
    ("Age at prediction date", pl.col("age_at_t").cut([40, 55, 70, 85], labels=AGE_LABELS).cast(pl.String), AGE_LABELS),
    ("Gender", pl.col("gender").fill_null("Unknown"), ["Female", "Male", "Unknown"]),
    ("Lives in Utah", pl.when(pl.col("address_state") == "UT").then(pl.lit("yes")).otherwise(pl.lit("no")), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Spouse on file", pl.when(pl.col("spouse_constituent_id").is_not_null()).then(pl.lit("yes")).otherwise(pl.lit("no")), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Constituent type (sensitivity only)", pl.col("type_group"), ["Friends", "Donors", "Alumni", "other University affiliation"]),
]
demo_signals = signal_table(feat_snap, demo_specs)

def dci(feature, level, never=False):
    return ci(feature, level, never, tbl=demo_signals)

type_tenure = (
    feat_snap.group_by("type_group")
    .agg(median_years_since_first_gift=pl.col("years_since_first_gift").median(),
         first_gift_before_fy2021=(pl.col("t") - pl.col("years_since_first_gift") + 1 < 2021).mean())
)
tt = {r["type_group"]: r for r in type_tenure.iter_rows(named=True)}

show(display_signals(demo_signals), pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="Usable constituent fields within prior-year bands, 12 month outcome")
```

- **Age** matters mainly at the young end. Donors 40 and under at the prediction date convert at `{python} dci("Age at prediction date", "40 or under")` times their expected rate (`{python} dci("Age at prediction date", "40 or under", never=True)` for never-major donors). The older groups are near or slightly above 1, with intervals that include 1, and the never-major pattern across them is not steady.
- **Gender** matters mainly through the Unknown group, at `{python} dci("Gender", "Unknown")`. Unknown gender may mark thinner records, so it is kept as its own level.
- **State and spouse on file** make little difference (`{python} dci("Lives in Utah", "yes")` for Utah residents and `{python} dci("Spouse on file", "yes")` for donors with a spouse on file).
- **Constituent type** separates Friends (`{python} dci("Constituent type (sensitivity only)", "Friends")`) from Donors (`{python} dci("Constituent type (sensitivity only)", "Donors")`), but it also tracks giving history: `{python} pct(tt["Friends"]["first_gift_before_fy2021"], 0)` of Friends donor-years belong to people whose first gift came before FY2021, compared with `{python} pct(tt["Donors"]["first_gift_before_fy2021"], 0)` for Donors. It probably repeats the tenure and legacy features, which supports leaving it out of the main model and testing it only as a sensitivity check.

### Leakage Rules

```{python}
#| label: soft-credit-leak

# soft credits in the outcome year among 12 month converters
conv12 = feat12.filter("converted").select("constituent_id", "t", "soft_in_t", "soft_before")
outcome_soft = conv12.join(person_years.select("constituent_id", t=pl.col("fy") - 1, soft_outcome=pl.col("soft_amt") > 0),
                           on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left").with_columns(pl.col("soft_outcome").fill_null(False))
soft_in_outcome = outcome_soft["soft_outcome"].mean()
soft_first_in_outcome = (outcome_soft["soft_outcome"] & ~outcome_soft["soft_in_t"] & ~outcome_soft["soft_before"]).mean()
```

Soft credits are the clearest case of timing leakage in the giving data. `{python} pct(soft_in_outcome)` of 12 month converters have a soft credit in the year they become major, and for `{python} pct(soft_first_in_outcome)` it is their first soft credit. Lifetime soft credit counts would therefore look very strong if they were not cut off at FY t. The table collects every leakage rule in this notebook.

| Source | Rule for a FY t snapshot | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Major donor class, annual giving group, sustainer flag | Dropped | Rebuilt from FY2026 giving |
| UofU lifetime fundraising, previous FY cash, committed giving | Dropped | Include or code PBS giving through FY2025 or FY2026 |
| Payments, soft credits, legacy gifts, gift types | Gifts dated on or before June 30 of FY t | Outcome-year gifts are the outcome, and most converters receive a soft credit in the conversion year |
| Solicitations and responses | FY t and earlier | Converters are solicited less in the outcome year, and responses are outcome-year payments |
| Passport viewing | FY t and earlier | Outcome-year viewing is not known at the prediction date |
| Age | Shifted to FY t | The snapshot age is measured in FY2026 |
| Cultivation selection and contact | Covered in the next section | Officers select donors partly on the information the model would use |

: Leakage rules for a FY t snapshot

### Summary for Modeling

- **Drop:** major donor class, annual giving group, the sustainer flag, and all three UofU dollar fields. Each is built from PBS giving through FY2025 or FY2026.
- **Use:** age shifted to the prediction date, which mainly flags younger donors, and gender with Unknown as its own level. State and spouse on file can be included but add little.
- **Sensitivity only:** constituent type, which largely repeats giving history.
- **No outside capacity measure** is available, so the model has to rely on PBS giving history. The business problem statement should say so.
- **Household rule:** the snapshot classification does not combine spouses, which should be confirmed with PBS.

## Cultivation Program

From FY2022 to FY2025, each of eight officer portfolios selected 125 donors a year. Within each portfolio, about three quarters of the selected donors were contacted and the rest were randomly held out. Portfolios also adopted a cultivation program at different times. Contact may change who becomes a major donor, which affects the outcome the model learns from, and the random holdout gives a fair way to measure that effect. Following decision 8, this section measures the effect and sets how contacted donors are handled. It does not build an uplift or operational model.

### How the Program Was Run

```{python}
#| label: cultivation-setup

cult = (
    clean["cultivation"].rename({"synthetic_id": "constituent_id", "fiscal_year": "t"})
    .join(clean["portfolios"].select("portfolio_id", "rollout_fy"), on="portfolio_id", how="left")
)
cult_summary = (
    cult.group_by("t")
    .agg(selected=pl.len(), contacted=pl.col("contacted").sum(), held_out=pl.col("holdout").sum(),
         in_adopting_portfolios=pl.col("program_adopted").sum())
    .sort("t")
)
adoption_matches_rollout = (cult["program_adopted"] == (cult["t"] >= cult["rollout_fy"].fill_null(9999))).mean()
selected_people = cult["constituent_id"].n_unique()

# the assignment year lines up with cohort t: selected donors gave in FY t and were not major
cult_year = cult.join(person_years.select("constituent_id", t=pl.col("fy"), total_t=pl.col("total"), major_t=pl.col("major")),
                      on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left")
gave_in_assignment_year = (cult_year["total_t"].fill_null(0) > 0).mean()
major_in_assignment_year = cult_year["major_t"].fill_null(False).mean()

show(cult_summary, caption="Cultivation selections, contacts, and holdouts by year")
```

Each year 1,000 donors were selected, and program adoption follows the rollout year in the portfolio table exactly (`{python} pct(adoption_matches_rollout)` agreement): two portfolios adopted in FY2023, two in FY2024, two in FY2025, one in FY2026 after the program window, and one never. Over the four years `{python} n(selected_people)` different people were selected. `{python} pct(gave_in_assignment_year)` of selected donors gave in their assignment year and `{python} pct(major_in_assignment_year)` were major that year, so a donor assigned in FY t is an eligible donor at the end of FY t, and the outcome is whether they become major in FY t+1. Each assignment year is matched to the cohort with the same t.

### Who Gets Selected

```{python}
#| label: cultivation-selection

feat_cult = with_features(active.filter((pl.col("window") == 1) & pl.col("t").is_between(2022, 2025))).join(
    cult.select("constituent_id", "t", "contacted", "program_adopted"), on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left"
).with_columns(
    group=pl.when(pl.col("contacted").is_null()).then(pl.lit("not selected"))
        .when(pl.col("contacted")).then(pl.lit("selected, contacted")).otherwise(pl.lit("selected, held out")),
    prior_rank=pl.col("prior_total").rank(descending=True).over("t") / pl.len().over("t"),
)
selected_in_eligible = cult.join(feat_cult.select("constituent_id", "t"), on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="semi").height / cult.height
selected_share = feat_cult["contacted"].is_not_null().mean()
median_rank_selected = feat_cult.filter(pl.col("contacted").is_not_null())["prior_rank"].median()

selection_profile = (
    feat_cult.group_by("group")
    .agg(donor_years=pl.len(), median_prior_year_giving=pl.col("prior_total").median(),
         former_major=pl.col("former_major").mean(), gave_5_of_5_years=(pl.col("years_last5") == 5).mean(),
         soft_credit_before=pl.col("soft_before").mean(), converted_next_year=pl.col("converted").mean())
    .sort("group")
)
show(selection_profile, pct_cols=["former_major", "gave_5_of_5_years", "soft_credit_before", "converted_next_year"], pct_digits=2, caption="Selected, held-out, and non-selected donors compared, FY2022 to FY2025 cohorts")
```

Selection draws from the eligible population (`{python} pct(selected_in_eligible)` of selected donors are eligible in their cohort) and covers about `{python} pct(selected_share)` of it each year. Officers pick from the top of the giving distribution: the median selected donor ranks in the top `{python} pct(median_rank_selected)` of eligible donors by prior-year giving. Selected donors are also more often former major donors, consistent givers, and past soft credit recipients. The contacted and held-out groups look alike on every measure, as random assignment should produce.

The within-band test shows whether officers see more than prior-year giving. Contacted donors are left out, because contact raised their conversion and would inflate the band rates. That leaves the held-out donors, who were selected the same way but never contacted, and the donors who were not selected. The table uses the FY2022 to FY2024 cohorts.

```{python}
#| label: selection-within-band

cult_val = feat_cult.filter(pl.col("in_validation"))
uncontacted = cult_val.filter(pl.col("group") != "selected, contacted")
cult_specs = [("Cultivation group", pl.col("group"), ["not selected", "selected, held out"])]
cult_signals = signal_table(uncontacted, cult_specs)
held_top_band = uncontacted.filter(pl.col("group") == "selected, held out")["band"].is_in(["$241 to $500", "over $500"]).mean()
show(display_signals(cult_signals), pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="Held-out compared with non-selected donors within prior-year bands, contacted donors left out")
```

Among donors who were not contacted, held-out donors convert at `{python} ci("Cultivation group", "selected, held out", tbl=cult_signals)` times the rate their prior-year giving predicts, so officers select on more than giving level even before contact. Among never-major donors the ratio is `{python} ci("Cultivation group", "selected, held out", never=True, tbl=cult_signals)`, with an interval that includes 1, so part of what officers see may be former major status. Selection also leans on giving: `{python} pct(held_top_band, 0)` of held-out donor-years gave more than $240 in FY t, compared with `{python} pct(all_top)` of all eligible donor-years. Officer selection is therefore a demanding benchmark for the model, which the baselines section measures directly.

### Effect of Contact

The held-out donors were selected the same way as the contacted donors, so the difference in their conversion rates estimates what contact itself does. Intervals use the couple-clustered bootstrap. Following decision 9, the main estimates use the FY2022 to FY2024 cohorts, and the FY2025 cohort, whose outcomes fall in FY2026, is shown once on its own.

```{python}
#| label: contact-effect

def clustered_diff(df, reps=1000, seed=20261009):
    # contacted minus held-out conversion rate, resampling couples with replacement
    g = df.group_by("couple_id").agg(
        n1=pl.col("contacted").sum(), c1=(pl.col("contacted") & pl.col("converted")).sum(),
        n0=(~pl.col("contacted")).sum(), c0=(~pl.col("contacted") & pl.col("converted")).sum(),
    ).sort("couple_id")
    n1, c1, n0, c0 = (g[c].to_numpy() for c in ("n1", "c1", "n0", "c0"))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    m = len(g)
    draws = np.empty(reps)
    for r in range(reps):
        k = rng.integers(0, m, m)
        draws[r] = c1[k].sum() / n1[k].sum() - c0[k].sum() / n0[k].sum()
    return c1.sum() / n1.sum(), c0.sum() / n0.sum(), np.quantile(draws, 0.025), np.quantile(draws, 0.975), int(n1.sum()), int(n0.sum())

selected = feat_cult.filter(pl.col("contacted").is_not_null())
sel_val = selected.filter("in_validation")
effect_specs = [
    ("all selected donors", "FY2022 to FY2024", sel_val),
    ("before program adoption", "FY2022 to FY2024", sel_val.filter(~pl.col("program_adopted"))),
    ("after program adoption", "FY2022 to FY2024", sel_val.filter(pl.col("program_adopted"))),
    ("never-major donors", "FY2022 to FY2024", sel_val.filter(~pl.col("former_major"))),
    ("all selected donors (labeled check)", "FY2025", selected.filter(pl.col("t") == 2025)),
]
effect_rows = []
for group, cohorts_used, df in effect_specs:
    p1, p0, lo, hi, n1_, n0_ = clustered_diff(df)
    effect_rows.append({"group": group, "cohorts": cohorts_used, "contacted": n1_, "contacted_rate": p1,
                        "held_out": n0_, "held_out_rate": p0, "difference": p1 - p0, "ci_low": lo, "ci_high": hi})
effects = pl.DataFrame(effect_rows)
eff = {r["group"]: r for r in effects.iter_rows(named=True)}
show(effects, pct_cols=["contacted_rate", "held_out_rate", "difference", "ci_low", "ci_high"], pct_digits=2, caption="Contacted minus held-out conversion, with couple-clustered 95% intervals")
```

```{python}
#| label: effect-text
e_all, e_before, e_after = eff["all selected donors"], eff["before program adoption"], eff["after program adoption"]
e_never, e_25 = eff["never-major donors"], eff["all selected donors (labeled check)"]
# describe where the before-adoption interval sits relative to zero
before_zero_text = ("just touching zero" if abs(e_before["ci_low"]) < 0.0005
                    else "including zero" if e_before["ci_low"] < 0 else "excluding zero")
```

Contact raises conversion. Across the FY2022 to FY2024 cohorts, contacted donors convert at `{python} pct(e_all["contacted_rate"], 2)` and held-out donors at `{python} pct(e_all["held_out_rate"], 2)`, a difference of `{python} pp(e_all["difference"])` percentage points (95% interval `{python} pp(e_all["ci_low"])` to `{python} pp(e_all["ci_high"])`). Following Kate's EDA, the table splits the effect by whether the portfolio had adopted the program. Before adoption the difference is `{python} pp(e_before["difference"])` points (`{python} pp(e_before["ci_low"])` to `{python} pp(e_before["ci_high"])`, `{python} before_zero_text`), and after adoption it is `{python} pp(e_after["difference"])` points (`{python} pp(e_after["ci_low"])` to `{python} pp(e_after["ci_high"])`), from only `{python} n(e_after["contacted"] + e_after["held_out"])` donor-years. Among never-major donors the difference is `{python} pp(e_never["difference"])` points (`{python} pp(e_never["ci_low"])` to `{python} pp(e_never["ci_high"])`). In the FY2025 cohort, contacted donors converted at `{python} pct(e_25["contacted_rate"], 2)` and held-out donors at `{python} pct(e_25["held_out_rate"], 2)`. The held-out rate in that cohort is higher than in any earlier one, and since those donors were never contacted, part of the FY2026 rise comes from donors themselves, which the next section examines.

### How Much Conversion Runs Through the Program

```{python}
#| label: cultivation-share

def program_share(t):
    # new major donors in FY t+1 (major in t+1, not in t) and whether they were selected or contacted in FY t
    new_next = (
        person_years.filter((pl.col("fy") == t + 1) & pl.col("major")).select("constituent_id")
        .join(person_years.filter((pl.col("fy") == t) & pl.col("major")), on="constituent_id", how="anti")
    )
    sel_t = cult.filter(pl.col("t") == t)
    return {"cohort": t, "new_majors_next_year": new_next.height,
            "selected_in_fy_t": new_next.join(sel_t, on="constituent_id", how="semi").height,
            "contacted_in_fy_t": new_next.join(sel_t.filter("contacted"), on="constituent_id", how="semi").height}

program_shares = pl.DataFrame([program_share(t) for t in range(2022, 2026)])
ps_val = program_shares.filter(pl.col("cohort") <= 2024).select(pl.exclude("cohort").sum()).row(0, named=True)
contacted_conv_share = cult_val.filter(pl.col("group") == "selected, contacted")["converted"].sum() / cult_val["converted"].sum()
contact_attrib = ps_val["contacted_in_fy_t"] * (1 - e_all["held_out_rate"] / e_all["contacted_rate"])
show(program_shares, caption="New major donors who were selected or contacted the year before")
```

Of the `{python} n(ps_val["new_majors_next_year"])` new major donors in FY2023 to FY2025, `{python} n(ps_val["selected_in_fy_t"])` (`{python} pct(ps_val["selected_in_fy_t"] / ps_val["new_majors_next_year"])`) had been selected the year before and `{python} n(ps_val["contacted_in_fy_t"])` had been contacted. Using the held-out rate as what would have happened without contact, roughly `{python} n(contact_attrib)` of those contacted conversions can be credited to contact. This is a rough figure, but it means part of the outcome in these years was produced by staff action.

### Handling Contacted Donors

For FY2022 to FY2024, contacted donors include `{python} pct(contacted_conv_share, 0)` of all 12 month converters, so dropping them would remove a large share of the positive cases. Following decision 8:

- **Training only.** Two flags, contacted in FY t and selected but held out in FY t, are added in training so the model can separate the effect of contact from donor potential.
- **Scoring.** Every donor is scored with both flags off, so lists rank donors on their own potential.
- **Reporting.** Results are reported for all eligible donors and for donors who were not contacted, since contact inflates the measured recall of any ranking for the FY2022 to FY2025 cohorts.
- **Officer benchmark.** Officer selection is compared with the model on held-out donors only, where contact has not changed the outcome.

### Summary for Modeling

- Officers select about `{python} pct(selected_share, 0)` of eligible donors a year, and held-out donors convert well above what their giving predicts, so officer selection is a strong benchmark. For never-major donors this is less certain.
- Contact raises conversion by about `{python} pp(e_all["difference"], 1)` percentage points across the validation cohorts. The effect looks larger after program adoption, as Kate found, but the after-adoption estimate rests on only `{python} n(e_after["contacted"] + e_after["held_out"])` donor-years.
- Part of the outcome in FY2023 to FY2025 comes from contact, so contact flags are used in training only and results are also reported for donors who were not contacted.

## The FY2026 Influx

Federal funding for public broadcasting ended in 2025, and FY2026 (July 2025 to June 2026) is the first full year after the cut. The business problem names the resulting influx of donations as a risk, because the last year may not look like the years a model learns from. This section describes what changed in FY2026, separates the donors' own response from the cultivation program, and checks the decision to keep the FY2025 cohort, whose outcomes fall in FY2026, out of validation.

### What Changed in FY2026

```{python}
#| label: influx-donors

first_gift = person_years.group_by("constituent_id").agg(first_fy=pl.col("fy").min())
donor_kind = (
    person_years.filter(pl.col("fy") >= 2020).select("constituent_id", "fy", "total")
    .join(first_gift, on="constituent_id")
    .sort("constituent_id", "fy")
    .with_columns(prev_fy=pl.col("fy").shift(1).over("constituent_id"), prev_total=pl.col("total").shift(1).over("constituent_id"))
    .filter(pl.col("fy") >= 2021)
    .with_columns(kind=pl.when(pl.col("first_fy") == pl.col("fy")).then(pl.lit("first gift"))
                  .when(pl.col("prev_fy") == pl.col("fy") - 1).then(pl.lit("gave last year"))
                  .otherwise(pl.lit("returning after a gap")))
)
kind_by_year = (
    donor_kind.group_by("fy").agg(
        first_gift=(pl.col("kind") == "first gift").sum(),
        gave_last_year=(pl.col("kind") == "gave last year").sum(),
        returning_after_gap=(pl.col("kind") == "returning after a gap").sum(),
        median_first_gift=pl.col("total").filter(pl.col("kind") == "first gift").median(),
    ).sort("fy")
)
retained = (
    donor_kind.filter(pl.col("kind") == "gave last year").group_by("fy")
    .agg(retained_donors=pl.len(), gave_more=(pl.col("total") > pl.col("prev_total")).mean(),
         gave_less=(pl.col("total") < pl.col("prev_total")).mean(), net_change=(pl.col("total") - pl.col("prev_total")).sum())
    .sort("fy")
)
kb = {r["fy"]: r for r in kind_by_year.iter_rows(named=True)}
rt = {r["fy"]: r for r in retained.iter_rows(named=True)}
rt_before = retained.filter(pl.col("fy") < 2026)
show(kind_by_year, caption="First-time, retained, and returning donors by fiscal year")
```

```{python}
#| label: influx-retained
show(retained, pct_cols=["gave_more", "gave_less"], caption="Change in giving among donors who also gave the year before")
```

The influx shows up in three places:

- **First-time donors nearly doubled**, from `{python} n(kb[2025]["first_gift"])` in FY2025 to `{python} n(kb[2026]["first_gift"])` in FY2026. Their median first-year giving stayed at `{python} usd(kb[2026]["median_first_gift"])`, `{python} "the same as in every earlier year" if kind_by_year["median_first_gift"].n_unique() == 1 else "close to earlier years"`, so these are more donors of the usual size rather than larger gifts.
- **Returning donors gave more.** Among donors who also gave the year before, `{python} pct(rt[2026]["gave_more"])` increased their giving in FY2026, compared with `{python} pct(rt_before["gave_more"].min())` to `{python} pct(rt_before["gave_more"].max())` in earlier years, and their net change was `{python} usd(rt[2026]["net_change"])` after being `{python} "negative in every earlier Unite year" if (rt_before["net_change"] < 0).all() else "mixed in earlier years"`.
- **More lapsed donors came back**: `{python} n(kb[2026]["returning_after_gap"])` in FY2026, up from `{python} n(kb[2025]["returning_after_gap"])`.

### Conversion in FY2026

The FY2025 cohort is the one whose 12 month outcome falls in FY2026. It is also the cohort with the most portfolios using the cultivation program, so a rise in conversion could come from either source. The held-out donors separate the two, since they were selected but never contacted.

```{python}
#| label: influx-conversion

active12 = active.filter(pl.col("window") == 1)
cohort_rows = []
for t in range(2021, 2026):
    d = active12.filter(pl.col("t") == t)
    est, lo, hi = clustered_rate(d)
    cohort_rows.append({"cohort": t, "outcome_year": t + 1, "eligible": d.height, "converters": int(d["converted"].sum()),
                        "rate": est, "ci_low": lo, "ci_high": hi,
                        "never_major_rate": d.filter(~pl.col("former_major"))["converted"].mean()})
by_cohort = pl.DataFrame(cohort_rows)
bc = {r["cohort"]: r for r in by_cohort.iter_rows(named=True)}
bc_before = by_cohort.filter(pl.col("cohort") < 2025)
show(by_cohort, pct_cols=["rate", "ci_low", "ci_high", "never_major_rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="12 month conversion by cohort with couple-clustered 95% intervals")
```

```{python}
#| label: cohort-plot
#| fig-height: 3.5

cohort_pd = by_cohort.with_columns(

With `{python} n(cp["FY2025 cohort"]["converters"])` converters these differences are uncertain, but they point the same way: after the cut, more conversions came from donors lower in the giving range, and more converters went straight to $2,000 or more.

```{python}
#| label: influx-ranking

def top_k_recall(df, col, k):
    # expected recall in the top k by col, with ties at the cutoff split evenly
    df = df.sort(col, descending=True)
    total = df["converted"].sum()
    if total == 0 or k >= df.height:
        return None
    cut = df[col][k - 1]
    above = df.filter(pl.col(col) > cut)
    tied = df.filter(pl.col(col) == cut)
    return (above["converted"].sum() + tied["converted"].sum() * (k - above.height) / tied.height) / total

ranking_rows = []
for t in range(2021, 2026):
    d = active12.filter(pl.col("t") == t)
    ranking_rows.append({"cohort": t, "converters": int(d["converted"].sum()),
                         "recall_top_1000": top_k_recall(d, "prior_total", 1000),
                         "never_major_recall_top_1000": top_k_recall(d.filter(~pl.col("former_major")), "prior_total", 1000)})
ranking_by_cohort = pl.DataFrame(ranking_rows)
rk = {r["cohort"]: r for r in ranking_by_cohort.iter_rows(named=True)}
rk_before = ranking_by_cohort.filter(pl.col("cohort") < 2025)
show(ranking_by_cohort, pct_cols=["recall_top_1000", "never_major_recall_top_1000"], caption="Recall at 1,000 for the prior-year ranking, by cohort")
```

Ranking donors by prior-year giving, the baseline the model has to beat, finds `{python} pct(rk[2025]["recall_top_1000"])` of FY2025 converters in the top 1,000, at the low end of the earlier cohorts (`{python} pct(rk_before["recall_top_1000"].min())` to `{python} pct(rk_before["recall_top_1000"].max())`). So the influx raised the level of conversion and shifted the mix somewhat, but the simple ranking still works about as well. Both points support decision 9. The FY2025 cohort adds converters for final training, but its higher base rate and different mix would distort comparisons between models.

### Summary for Modeling

- FY2026 brought more first-time donors, more returning donors, and higher giving from existing donors.
- Conversion rose among held-out donors who were never contacted, which suggests the rise is partly the donors' own response to the funding cut, although the evidence rests on few converters.
- The influx raised the conversion rate and shifted converters toward donors lower in the giving range, but the prior-year ranking still works about as well. The FY2025 cohort is used in final training and reported once as a labeled check, not for model selection (decision 9).

## Baselines

The model has to show that it finds future major donors better than simple rules PBS Utah could already use. Following decision 10, every baseline is scored the same way: each validation cohort is ranked, the top 1,000 donors form the list (about what the cultivation program can work in a year), and we report the share of converters on the list (recall), the share of the list that converts (precision), and precision divided by the base rate (lift). Ties at the cutoff are split evenly, so a rule that picks fewer than 1,000 donors fills the rest of the list at random. Results are pooled over the FY2021 to FY2024 cohorts, with couple-clustered intervals.

The baselines are:

- **Prior-year giving:** donors ranked by their FY t giving. This is the bar to beat.
- **Recency, frequency, and value (RFV):** the classic score named in the business problem, the sum of three 1 to 5 scores: days since the last gift (quintiles within the cohort, most recent = 5), years given in the last five, and FY t giving (quintiles).
- **Threshold rules from Erin's EDA:** gave $500 or more in FY t, and gave $1,000 or more over FY t-2 to FY t.
- **Former major or $500:** a rule that adds the strongest signal from the giving history section to the first threshold.
- **Officer selection:** the donors officers chose, measured only where contact has not changed the outcome (explained below).

```{python}
#| label: baseline-setup

def quintile(col, descending=False):
    # 1 to 5 score from the within-cohort percentile rank, with ties sharing a rank
    pct_rank = pl.col(col).rank("average", descending=descending) / pl.len()
    return (pct_rank * 5).ceil().clip(1, 5).cast(pl.Int32).over("t")

def add_scores(df):
    return df.with_columns(
        rfv=quintile("days_since_last_gift", descending=True) + pl.col("years_last5").cast(pl.Int32) + quintile("prior_total"),
        rule_500=(pl.col("prior_total") >= 500).cast(pl.Int32),
        rule_3yr_1000=((pl.col("prior_total") + pl.col("two_years_before")) >= 1000).cast(pl.Int32),
        rule_former_or_500=(pl.col("former_major") | (pl.col("prior_total") >= 500)).cast(pl.Int32),
    )

BASELINES = {
    "prior-year giving": "prior_total",
    "RFV score": "rfv",
    "rule: $500 or more in FY t": "rule_500",
    "rule: $1,000 or more over three years": "rule_3yr_1000",
    "rule: former major or $500 or more": "rule_former_or_500",
}
K = 1000

def ranked(df, col):
    # per cohort, rows sorted by score with a group id for each tied score
    parts = []
    for t in sorted(df["t"].unique().to_list()):
        d = df.filter(pl.col("t") == t).sort(col, descending=True)
        gid = (d[col].rank("dense", descending=True) - 1).cast(pl.Int64).to_numpy()
        parts.append((d["couple_id"], d["converted"].to_numpy().astype(float), d["w"].to_numpy().astype(float), gid))
    return parts

def hits_at_k(conv, w, gid, k):
    # expected converters in the top k by weight, splitting the tied group at the cutoff evenly
    gw = np.bincount(gid, weights=w)
    gc = np.bincount(gid, weights=w * conv)
    cum = np.cumsum(gw)
    g = np.searchsorted(cum, k)
    if g >= len(gw):
        return gc.sum()
    return gc[:g].sum() + gc[g] * (k - (cum[g] - gw[g])) / gw[g]

def evaluate(df, scores, k=K, reps=1000, seed=20261009):
    # pooled recall, precision, and lift at k with couple-clustered bootstrap intervals
    couples = df["couple_id"].unique().sort()
    lists = {name: [(couples.search_sorted(c).to_numpy(), conv, w, gid) for c, conv, w, gid in ranked(df, col)]
             for name, col in scores.items()}
    n_cohorts = df["t"].n_unique()

    def metrics(mult):
        out = {}
        for name, parts in lists.items():
            hits = conv_total = weight_total = 0.0
            for ci_, conv, w, gid in parts:
                ww = w if mult is None else w * mult[ci_]
                hits += hits_at_k(conv, ww, gid, k)
                conv_total += (ww * conv).sum()
                weight_total += ww.sum()
            precision = hits / (k * n_cohorts)
            out[name] = (hits / conv_total, precision, precision / (conv_total / weight_total))
        return out

    point = metrics(None)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    m = len(couples)
    draws = {name: [] for name in scores}
    for _ in range(reps):
        mult = np.bincount(rng.integers(0, m, m), minlength=m).astype(float)
        for name, vals in metrics(mult).items():
            draws[name].append(vals)
    rows = []
    for name in scores:
        d = np.array(draws[name])
        lo, hi = np.quantile(d, [0.025, 0.975], axis=0)
        r, p, l = point[name]
        rows.append({"baseline": name, "recall": r, "recall_low": lo[0], "recall_high": hi[0],
                     "precision": p, "lift": round(l, 1), "lift_low": round(lo[2], 1), "lift_high": round(hi[2], 1)})
    return pl.DataFrame(rows)

scored12 = add_scores(feat12).with_columns(w=pl.lit(1.0))
```
