```{python}
bn = {r["baseline"]: r for r in base_never.iter_rows(named=True)}
```



A random list of 1,000 would hold about `{python} pct(random_recall)` of converters. Ranking by prior-year giving holds `{python} pct(ba["prior-year giving"]["recall"])` (95% interval `{python} pct(ba["prior-year giving"]["recall_low"])` to `{python} pct(ba["prior-year giving"]["recall_high"])`), with a precision of `{python} pct(ba["prior-year giving"]["precision"], 2)`, about `{python} f'{ba["prior-year giving"]["lift"]:.0f}'` times the base rate. Among never-major donors it holds `{python} pct(bn["prior-year giving"]["recall"])`. The other baselines compare as follows:

- **RFV** is clearly weaker, at `{python} pct(ba["RFV score"]["recall"])` overall and `{python} pct(bn["RFV score"]["recall"])` for never-major donors. Its value quintile lumps together everyone in the top fifth of giving, and its recency part rewards monthly sustainers, who convert less than their giving predicts (giving history section).
- **The $500 rule** reaches `{python} pct(ba["rule: $500 or more in FY t"]["recall"])`. It picks about `{python} n(rule_500_size)` donors a year and fills the rest of the list at random, while the prior-year ranking fills those places from the $241 to $500 band, which explains most of the gap. **The three-year rule** reaches `{python} pct(ba["rule: $1,000 or more over three years"]["recall"])`.
- **Former major or $500** reaches `{python} pct(ba["rule: former major or $500 or more"]["recall"])`, the same as the prior-year ranking within the uncertainty. For never-major donors the former major part has no effect, so it matches the $500 rule.

### Officer Selection Without Contact

Officers chose about 1,000 donors a year from FY2022 to FY2024, but contact raised the conversion of the three quarters who were contacted, so their observed outcomes would flatter both officer selection and any ranking that puts them near the top. The held-out donors are a random quarter of the officers' choices. Dropping the contacted donors and counting each held-out donor `{python} f'{(1000 / 248):.2f}'` times (1,000 selected over 248 held out) rebuilds the eligible pool as it would have looked without contact. All baselines, including officer selection, are scored on that pool.

```{python}
#| label: baselines-no-contact

held_weight = (
    cult.filter(pl.col("t").is_between(2022, 2024)).group_by("t")
    .agg(w_held=pl.len() / pl.col("holdout").sum())
)
no_contact = (
    add_scores(feat_cult.filter(pl.col("in_validation")))
    .filter(pl.col("group") != "selected, contacted")
    .join(held_weight, on="t", how="left")
    .with_columns(
        w=pl.when(pl.col("group") == "selected, held out").then(pl.col("w_held")).otherwise(pl.lit(1.0)),
        officer=(pl.col("group") == "selected, held out").cast(pl.Int32),
    )
)
NO_CONTACT_BASELINES = {"officer selection": "officer", **BASELINES}
base_nc = evaluate(no_contact, NO_CONTACT_BASELINES)
base_nc_never = evaluate(no_contact.filter(~pl.col("former_major")), NO_CONTACT_BASELINES)
nc_table = pl.concat([
    base_nc.with_columns(group=pl.lit("all eligible")),
    base_nc_never.with_columns(group=pl.lit("never major")),
]).select("group", "baseline", "recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision", "lift", "lift_low", "lift_high")
nc = {r["baseline"]: r for r in base_nc.iter_rows(named=True)}
ncn = {r["baseline"]: r for r in base_nc_never.iter_rows(named=True)}
show(nc_table, pct_cols=["recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision"], caption="Baselines on the no-contact pool, including officer selection, FY2022 to FY2024 cohorts")
```

Without contact, officer selection holds `{python} pct(nc["officer selection"]["recall"])` of converters (`{python} pct(nc["officer selection"]["recall_low"])` to `{python} pct(nc["officer selection"]["recall_high"])`), compared with `{python} pct(nc["prior-year giving"]["recall"])` for the prior-year ranking and `{python} pct(nc["rule: former major or $500 or more"]["recall"])` for the former major or $500 rule. Among never-major donors the figures are `{python} pct(ncn["officer selection"]["recall"])`, `{python} pct(ncn["prior-year giving"]["recall"])`, and `{python} pct(ncn["rule: former major or $500 or more"]["recall"])`. The intervals for officer selection are wide because they rest on the `{python} n(no_contact.filter(pl.col("officer") == 1).height)` held-out donor-years. Overall, officers do about as well as the prior-year ranking, so a model that beats the ranking would also be competitive with current practice. Among never-major donors officers appear to do worse than the ranking, but the intervals overlap widely and officers may be choosing donors for reasons other than conversion within a year.

### Longer Outcome Windows

The 3 year outcome can be tested on the FY2021 and FY2022 cohorts. The 5 year outcome needs cohorts from FY2020 or earlier, before solicitation and Passport data begin, so it is tested with giving history only on the FY2011 to FY2020 cohorts.

```{python}
#| label: baselines-longer

LONG_BASELINES = {k: BASELINES[k] for k in ("prior-year giving", "RFV score", "rule: former major or $500 or more")}
scored3 = add_scores(feat3).with_columns(w=pl.lit(1.0))
c5 = cohorts.filter((pl.col("segment") == "active") & (pl.col("window") == 5) & pl.col("t").is_between(2011, 2020))
scored5 = add_scores(with_features(c5)).with_columns(w=pl.lit(1.0))
long_table = pl.concat([
    evaluate(scored3, LONG_BASELINES).with_columns(outcome=pl.lit("within 3 years"), cohorts=pl.lit("FY2021 to FY2022")),
    evaluate(scored5, LONG_BASELINES).with_columns(outcome=pl.lit("within 5 years"), cohorts=pl.lit("FY2011 to FY2020")),
]).select("outcome", "cohorts", "baseline", "recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision", "lift")
lt = {(r["outcome"], r["baseline"]): r for r in long_table.iter_rows(named=True)}
show(long_table, pct_cols=["recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision"], caption="Baselines for the 3 and 5 year outcomes")
```

The prior-year ranking holds `{python} pct(lt[("within 3 years", "prior-year giving")]["recall"])` of 3 year converters and `{python} pct(lt[("within 5 years", "prior-year giving")]["recall"])` of 5 year converters in the top 1,000. Recall falls as the window lengthens, so more of the eventual converters sit outside the top of the giving range, which leaves more room for a model to improve on the simple ranking. The former major or $500 rule does slightly better than the ranking at 3 years (`{python} pct(lt[("within 3 years", "rule: former major or $500 or more")]["recall"])`) but worse at 5 years (`{python} pct(lt[("within 5 years", "rule: former major or $500 or more")]["recall"])`). The 5 year cohorts come from the legacy years, when giving was recorded in a different system, so they show whether giving history alone carries over a long window rather than how a current model would perform.

### Summary for Modeling

- The bar to beat at a list of 1,000 is the prior-year ranking: `{python} pct(ba["prior-year giving"]["recall"])` recall for all eligible donors and `{python} pct(bn["prior-year giving"]["recall"])` for never-major donors over the FY2021 to FY2024 cohorts.
- The classic RFV score is much weaker and should be reported but not used as the main comparison.
- Simple threshold rules come close to the prior-year ranking, and the former major or $500 rule matches it at 12 months, which shows how much of the signal sits in giving level and former major status alone. The team agreed to keep the prior-year ranking as the main bar and to report the former major or $500 rule as a second check the model should also clear.
- Officer selection is compared on the no-contact pool, where it holds `{python} pct(nc["officer selection"]["recall"])` of converters against `{python} pct(nc["prior-year giving"]["recall"])` for the prior-year ranking, with wide intervals.
- The model's room to add value is largest for never-major donors and for the longer windows.

## Key Findings

This section pulls the results of the notebook together. The next section turns them into a plan for modeling.

### Data Problems and How They Were Handled

- **Copy rows.** `{python} n(audit["pay_copy_ids"].len())` Unite payments (`{python} usd(pay_copy_amt)`), `{python} n(audit["sc_exact_duplicates"] + audit["sc_copy_ids"].len())` soft credits, and `{python} n(audit["legacy_unlinked_copies"])` legacy rows were copies of valid rows. Content-based rules removed them, and the copy labels agree with the rules exactly (`{python} n(label_mismatches)` mismatches).
- **Double counting through organizations.** Organization payments equal the soft credits they fund in every year, so individual giving counts soft credits and leaves organization payments out.
- **Fields that describe the outcome.** Major donor class, annual giving group, the sustainer flag, and all three University of Utah dollar fields reflect PBS giving through FY2025 or FY2026. All are dropped, which leaves no outside measure of giving capacity.
- **Missing Passport years.** `{python} pct(no_passport, 0)` of eligible donor-years have no viewing record, and only `{python} pct(view_again.min(), 0)` to `{python} pct(view_again.max(), 0)` of a year's viewers appear the next year. Missing years are kept as their own level.
- **Staff action in the outcome.** Among donors officers selected, contact raised conversion by `{python} pp(e_all["difference"])` percentage points, so part of the outcome in FY2023 to FY2025 was produced by officers.
- **The FY2026 influx.** The FY2025 cohort converted at `{python} pct(bc[2025]["rate"], 3)` against `{python} pct(bc_before["rate"].min(), 3)` to `{python} pct(bc_before["rate"].max(), 3)` before, with a different mix of converters.
- **A definition to confirm.** PBS Utah's own classification counts the one couple that reaches $1,200 only in combination as two non-major donors, unlike the team's household rule.

### Strongest Relationships With the Target

- **Prior-year giving dominates.** Donors who gave more than $500 in FY t convert at `{python} pct(pb["over $500"]["rate"])` and supply `{python} pct(pb["over $500"]["share_of_converters"], 0)` of converters while being under 1% of eligible donor-years.
- **Former major status.** Across the FY2021 to FY2025 cohorts, former major donors are `{python} pct(r12_former["donor_years"] / r12["donor_years"])` of eligible donor-years but `{python} pct(r12_former["converters"] / r12["converters"], 0)` of converters, and they convert at `{python} f'{sig("Former major donor", "yes"):.1f}'` times what their giving predicts.
- **Length of giving history.** First-year donors and donors with no gift the year before convert at about a fifth of what their giving predicts.
- **Officer judgment.** Donors officers selected but never contacted convert at `{python} f'{sig("Cultivation group", "selected, held out", "ratio", cult_signals):.1f}'` times what their giving predicts, so officers see something beyond giving level.
- **Weak once giving is known:** upgrade gifts, soft credits in FY t, solicitation volume and responses, communication channel, having a Passport record, state, and spouse on file. Two signals are modest: heavy Passport viewers convert somewhat more than their giving predicts, and donors 40 and under convert less.

### What This Means for Modeling

- The 12 month outcome is rare (`{python} pct(r12["rate"], 2)`), so models are compared on recall, precision, and lift at a list of 1,000, never on accuracy.
- The bar is high. Prior-year giving alone holds `{python} pct(ba["prior-year giving"]["recall"], 0)` of converters in the top 1,000, and `{python} pct(bn["prior-year giving"]["recall"], 0)` for never-major donors, so the model's value has to show up as a gain over that ranking, most of all for never-major donors and the longer windows.
- Giving history is the core of the feature set. Engagement data adds little, so its main role is to be tested, not assumed.
- Validation has to respect time, spouses, contact, and the funding cut: rolling tests on FY2022 to FY2024, couples in the same fold, contact flags in training only, and the FY2025 cohort kept for final training and one labeled check.

## Modeling Recommendations

This section brings the earlier findings together into a plan for the modeling phase. It does not fit a model.

### Outcomes and Data

```{python}
#| label: outcome-plan

conv_by_window = {
    w: cohorts.filter((pl.col("segment") == "active") & (pl.col("window") == w) & (pl.col("t") >= 2021))
    for w in (1, 3, 5)
}
plan = pl.DataFrame([
    {"outcome": "12 months", "feature_set": "all features",
     "test_cohorts": "FY2022 to FY2024, one at a time", "labeled_check": "FY2025",
     "converters_in_fy2021_on_cohorts": int(conv_by_window[1]["converted"].sum())},
    {"outcome": "within 3 years", "feature_set": "giving history; all features as a secondary check",
     "test_cohorts": "legacy-era cohorts for giving history; FY2021 to FY2022 by grouped cross-validation for all features", "labeled_check": "FY2023 (outcomes through FY2026)",
     "converters_in_fy2021_on_cohorts": int(conv_by_window[3]["converted"].sum())},
    {"outcome": "within 5 years", "feature_set": "giving history only",
     "test_cohorts": "legacy-era cohorts through FY2020", "labeled_check": "FY2021 (outcomes through FY2026)",
     "converters_in_fy2021_on_cohorts": int(conv_by_window[5]["converted"].sum())},
])
show(plan, caption="Outcomes, feature sets, and test cohorts for the modeling phase")
```

- **12 month outcome (primary).** Becoming major in FY t+1 under the household rule, for active eligible donors. All features are available from FY2021, so this is the outcome the model is judged on.
- **3 and 5 year outcomes.** A strictly time-based test needs training cohorts whose outcomes were known before the test cohort's prediction date. For the 3 year outcome that means cohorts from FY2019 or earlier when testing FY2022, before solicitation and Passport data exist. The longer windows should therefore be modeled with giving history, which reaches back to FY1999 and, in the baselines section, still ranked `{python} pct(lt[("within 5 years", "prior-year giving")]["recall"], 0)` of 5 year converters into the top 1,000. A version with all features can be checked by grouped cross-validation on the FY2021 and FY2022 cohorts, reported as secondary. This matches the business problem's fallback of treating the longer window as a projection when the data spans too few years.
- **Tier.** Among predicted converters, the tier reached ($1,200, $2,000, or $5,000 and up). With only `{python} n(tier_n.get("$5,000+", 0))` converters at $5,000 and up, the top tier will be estimated poorly and should be reported with that caveat.
- **Lapsed segment.** With `{python} n(lapsed_conv)` converters in five cohorts, lapsed donors are reported separately with their base rate rather than modeled.

### Features

| Status | Features |
|---|---|
| Use | Prior-year giving, former major status, years given in the last five, years since first gift (with legacy years), legacy-era giving years, change from last year, giving in the two years before, largest gift share of FY t, sustainer status and monthly amount, soft credits before FY t, age at FY t, gender with Unknown as its own level |
| Test, expected to add little | Titles viewed and other Passport measures, recency (with sustainer status), upgrade and additional gifts, soft credits in FY t, solicitation counts, responses, and channels, state, spouse on file |
| Training only | Contacted in FY t, selected but held out in FY t (both off when scoring) |
| Sensitivity check only | Constituent type |
| Drop | Major donor class, annual giving group, sustainer flag, all UofU dollar fields, and anything dated after June 30 of FY t |

: Feature status for the modeling phase

Giving history is the core of the model. Tree-based models or explicit threshold features should handle the jumps in giving (exact tier amounts, the $600 cluster) better than linear terms in raw dollars. Every feature is built through the shared script so that the same cutoff at June 30 of FY t applies everywhere.

### Validation Design

- **Rolling time-based test.** For the 12 month outcome, train on all cohorts before the test cohort and test on one cohort at a time: FY2022 (trained on FY2021), FY2023, and FY2024. FY2021 is training only because no earlier cohort has all features.
- **Tuning inside the training years.** Hyperparameters are chosen by cross-validation within the training cohorts, grouped by couple so spouses stay in the same fold. The test cohort is never used for tuning.
- **FY2025 cohort.** Not used for model selection. After the model is chosen, it is trained on FY2021 to FY2024, tested once on FY2025 as a labeled check across the funding cut, and then retrained on FY2021 to FY2025 for the final list.
- **Class imbalance.** With a base rate near 0.15%, accuracy is meaningless. Class weights are fine, but any resampling must happen inside the training folds only.

### Measures and Reporting

- **Primary measure:** recall at a list of 1,000 per cohort, pooled across the test cohorts, with precision and lift at 1,000 alongside.
- **Secondary measures:** average precision over the whole ranking, recall at 1,000 for the longer windows, and a calibration check, since staff will see probabilities.
- **Groups:** all eligible donors, never-major donors, and the no-contact pool (contacted donors dropped and held-out donors reweighted), where officer selection is the comparison. The lapsed segment is reported separately.
- **Uncertainty:** couple-clustered bootstrap intervals for every rate, recall, and lift.

### What Success Looks Like

The model is compared with the baselines on the same test cohorts. The table gives the baseline numbers for FY2022 to FY2024, the three test cohorts in the rolling design.

```{python}
#| label: success-bars

bars_specs = {k: BASELINES[k] for k in ("prior-year giving", "rule: former major or $500 or more")}
test_scored = scored12.filter(pl.col("t") >= 2022)
bars = pl.concat([
    evaluate(test_scored, bars_specs).with_columns(group=pl.lit("all eligible")),
    evaluate(test_scored.filter(~pl.col("former_major")), bars_specs).with_columns(group=pl.lit("never major")),
]).select("group", "baseline", "recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision", "lift")
bar = {(r["group"], r["baseline"]): r for r in bars.iter_rows(named=True)}
show(bars, pct_cols=["recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision"], caption="Bars the model must clear on the FY2022 to FY2024 test cohorts")
```

The model succeeds if, on the FY2022 to FY2024 test cohorts, its recall at 1,000 is above the prior-year ranking's `{python} pct(bar[("all eligible", "prior-year giving")]["recall"])` for all eligible donors and `{python} pct(bar[("never major", "prior-year giving")]["recall"])` for never-major donors, and it also clears the former major or $500 rule. Because the baseline intervals are about `{python} pp((bar[("all eligible", "prior-year giving")]["recall_high"] - bar[("all eligible", "prior-year giving")]["recall_low"]) / 2, 1)` points wide on either side, the comparison should be made on the same bootstrap draws (the difference in recall between model and baseline), not by checking whether two separate intervals overlap. A gain among never-major donors matters most, since those are the donors staff are least likely to know already.

## Revisions to the Business Problem Statement

The team agreed to revise the business problem statement after the EDA (decision 14). The table lists each change, what the original statement said, and the evidence for the change. A tracked-changes version of the full statement is kept as a separate team document.

| Topic | Original statement | Revision | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Size of the major donor group | About 1% of the donor file and 19% of donor revenue | About `{python} pct(pooled_share["donors"], 1)` of donors and `{python} pct(pooled_share["revenue"], 0)` of individual giving, FY2021 to FY2026 | How Rare Major Giving Is |
| Major donor definition | Per individual | Per person, except that a couple reaching $1,200 only in combination counts as one major donor; to be confirmed with PBS Utah | Household Rule; PBS Classification Fields |
| Primary success measure | At least 25% of converters in the top 10% of the list | Recall at a list of 1,000, the cultivation program's annual capacity, for the 12 month outcome and, as a projection, the 3 to 5 year outcome | Baselines |
| Benchmark | Random selection and an RFV baseline | Beat the prior-year giving ranking (`{python} pct(ba["prior-year giving"]["recall"], 0)` recall at 1,000) and clear a "former major or $500" rule; also report RFV, officer selection, and random selection | Baselines |
| Reporting groups | All donors | All eligible donors, never-major donors, and donors not contacted by officers; lapsed donors reported separately | Conversion Base Rates; Cultivation Program |
| Giving tiers | $1,200, $2,000, $5,000, $10,000, $15,000+ | $1,200, $2,000, and $5,000+ (only `{python} n(tier_n.get("$5,000+", 0))` of the 12 month converters reach $5,000+) | Tiers Reached at Conversion |
| Inputs | Giving history, campaign and event participation, UofU engagement and capacity scores, Passport viewing | Giving history (including legacy years), soft credits, solicitation history, and Passport viewing. No UofU scores are in the data, and the UofU dollar fields encode PBS giving | Snapshot Fields and Leakage |
| Expected drivers | Giving, engagement, and viewing behaviors | Mainly giving history and former major status; solicitation and viewing add little once prior-year giving is known | Signals From Giving History; Solicitation and Passport Viewing |
| Validation | Time-based validation with a sensitivity test with and without the last year | Rolling time-based tests on FY2022 to FY2024, spouses in the same fold, contact flags in training only; the FY2025 cohort used only in final training and reported once as a labeled check | Modeling Recommendations; The FY2026 Influx |
| Longer window | Tested if the data spans enough years, otherwise a projection | Modeled with giving history and tested on legacy-era cohorts; an all-input 3 year version checked by grouped cross-validation | Modeling Recommendations |
| Risks | Leakage, incomplete Passport coverage, the donation influx | Adds snapshot-field leakage, the cultivation program's effect on outcomes, and an unusually large share of first-year donors in the next list | Snapshot Fields and Leakage; Cultivation Program; The FY2026 Influx |

: Changes to the business problem statement and their evidence

### Points to Confirm With PBS Utah

- **Household rule.** The snapshot's major donor class does not combine spouses, while the team's rule does. Only one couple is affected in this data, but the rule should be confirmed.
- **Former major donors.** They are about half of the converters. If officers already work these donors, the list's value comes mainly from never-major donors, which is why those results are reported separately.
- **Meaning of contact before program adoption.** Contact had a smaller effect before portfolios adopted the program, and it is not clear what contact involved in those years.
- **Missing Passport years.** Viewing records rarely carry over from one year to the next, and the data cannot show whether a missing year means no viewing, no linked account, or no consent.

```{python}
    {"component": "Python", "version": sys.version.split()[0]},
    {"component": "polars", "version": pl.__version__},

])
```

- **Data.** The repository includes `data_cache/`, the nine course tables converted to Parquet, and the notebook reads them from there, so the raw CSV files are not needed. To rebuild the cache from the raw release, put the nine CSV files in `../tables` relative to this notebook and delete `data_cache/`; the next render converts them again.
- **Build.** All cleaning, panel, cohort, and feature code lives in `build_panel.py`. The notebook only analyzes what the script builds.
- **Randomness.** Every bootstrap uses seed 20261009 and 1,000 resamples, and couples are sorted before resampling, so two renders give identical numbers.
- **Rendering.** `quarto render pbs_utah_group_eda.qmd`. The notebook was rendered with Quarto 1.10, and a full render took two to four minutes on a laptop, most of it in the bootstrap intervals.

### Checks on Claims in the Text

Several sentences in this notebook describe a direction or a comparison in words (for example, "an interval that includes 1" or "at the low end of the earlier cohorts"). The chunk below tests each of those claims against the numbers, so a change to the data or the build cannot leave the text saying something the numbers no longer support. The render stops if any check fails.

```{python}
#| label: claim-checks

def includes_one(tbl, feature, level, never=False):
    lo, hi = ("never_low", "never_high") if never else ("ci_low", "ci_high")
    return sig(feature, level, lo, tbl) <= 1 <= sig(feature, level, hi, tbl)

def excludes_one(tbl, feature, level, never=False):
    return not includes_one(tbl, feature, level, never)

others = signals12.filter(pl.col("converters") > 0).filter(
    ~((pl.col("feature") == "Former major donor") & (pl.col("level") == "yes"))
).sort("ratio", descending=True)
higher_than_former = others.filter(pl.col("ratio") > sig("Former major donor", "yes"))

claims = [
    # numbers written out in the Introduction, which comes before any code runs
    ("Introduction: major donors are about 0.3% of donors", round(100 * pooled_share["donors"], 1) == 0.3),
    ("Introduction: major donors give about 8% of individual giving", round(100 * pooled_share["revenue"]) == 8),
    ("Introduction: prior-year ranking holds about 75% at 1,000", round(100 * ba["prior-year giving"]["recall"]) == 75),
    ("Introduction: about half of converters are former major donors", 0.45 <= r12_former["converters"] / r12["converters"] <= 0.55),
    ("Key findings: donors over $500 are under 1% of eligible donor-years", pb["over $500"]["share_of_donors"] < 0.01),
    ("Missing values: Unknown gender is about a fifth of people", 0.18 <= missing.filter(pl.col("field") == "Gender = Unknown")["missing"][0] <= 0.23),
    ("Missing values: about half of eligible donor-years have no Passport record", 0.45 <= no_passport <= 0.55),
    ("Missing values: payment and soft credit tables have no nulls", payment_nulls == 0),
    ("Only 'gave less' has a higher within-band ratio than former major status",
     higher_than_former.select(pl.struct("feature", "level")).to_series().to_list() == [{"feature": "Change from last year", "level": "gave less"}]),
    ("Short histories are about a fifth of expected (all three between 0.15 and 0.25)",
     all(0.15 <= sig(f, l) <= 0.25 for f, l in [("Years since first gift", "1"), ("Years given, last 5", "1 of 5"), ("Change from last year", "no gift last year")])),
    ("Former-major-type signals include 1 among never-major donors",
     all(includes_one(signals12, f, l, True) for f, l in [("Change from last year", "gave less"), ("Giving in the two years before", "$1,200 or more"), ("Soft credit before FY t", "yes")])),
    ("Upgrade gifts and soft credits in FY t: never-major intervals include 1",
     includes_one(signals12, "Upgrade gift in FY t", "yes", True) and includes_one(signals12, "Soft credit in FY t", "yes", True)),
    ("Recency: most recent group below the over-180-day group within bands",
     sig("Days since last gift", "30 or less") < sig("Days since last gift", "over 180")),
    ("Most solicitation intervals include 1",
     np.mean([includes_one(sol_signals, r["feature"], r["level"]) for r in sol_signals.filter(pl.col("converters") > 0).iter_rows(named=True)]) > 0.5),
    ("Viewing record adds nothing (interval includes 1)", includes_one(pv_signals, "Viewing record in FY t", "yes")),
    ("Completion and genre breadth intervals include 1 at every level",
     all(includes_one(pv_signals, r["feature"], r["level"]) and includes_one(pv_signals, r["feature"], r["level"], True)
         for r in pv_signals.filter(pl.col("feature").is_in(["Genres viewed in FY t", "Share of titles watched"])).iter_rows(named=True))),
    ("Heavy viewers exclude 1 for all and never-major donors",
     excludes_one(pv_signals, "Titles viewed in FY t", "over 40") and excludes_one(pv_signals, "Titles viewed in FY t", "over 40", True)),
    ("Age: only the youngest group excludes 1",
     excludes_one(demo_signals, "Age at prediction date", "40 or under")
     and all(includes_one(demo_signals, "Age at prediction date", l) for l in ["41 to 55", "56 to 70", "71 to 85", "over 85"])),
    ("State and spouse intervals include 1",
     includes_one(demo_signals, "Lives in Utah", "yes") and includes_one(demo_signals, "Spouse on file", "yes")),
    ("Held-out donors exclude 1 overall and include 1 for never-major donors",
     excludes_one(cult_signals, "Cultivation group", "selected, held out") and includes_one(cult_signals, "Cultivation group", "selected, held out", True)),
    ("Contact effect interval excludes 0 for all selected donors", eff["all selected donors"]["ci_low"] > 0),
    ("Not-selected FY2025 rate is within 0.005 points of FY2022", abs(gy[(2025, "not selected")] - gy[(2022, "not selected")]) < 0.00005),
    ("FY2025 converter mix shifted in the stated directions",
     cp["FY2025 cohort"]["former_major"] < cp["FY2021 to FY2024 cohorts"]["former_major"]
     and cp["FY2025 cohort"]["gave_over_500_in_fy_t"] < cp["FY2021 to FY2024 cohorts"]["gave_over_500_in_fy_t"]
     and cp["FY2025 cohort"]["reached_2000_or_more"] > cp["FY2021 to FY2024 cohorts"]["reached_2000_or_more"]),
    ("FY2025 prior-year recall is at the low end of the earlier cohorts", rk[2025]["recall_top_1000"] <= rk_before["recall_top_1000"].median()),
    ("RFV recall is below the prior-year interval", ba["RFV score"]["recall"] < ba["prior-year giving"]["recall_low"]),
    ("Former major or $500 matches the prior-year ranking within its interval",
     ba["prior-year giving"]["recall_low"] <= ba["rule: former major or $500 or more"]["recall"] <= ba["prior-year giving"]["recall_high"]),
    ("Officer selection and prior-year ranking intervals overlap",
     nc["officer selection"]["recall_low"] <= nc["prior-year giving"]["recall"] <= nc["officer selection"]["recall_high"]),
    ("Former major or $500 beats the ranking at 3 years and trails at 5 years",
     lt[("within 3 years", "rule: former major or $500 or more")]["recall"] > lt[("within 3 years", "prior-year giving")]["recall"]
     and lt[("within 5 years", "rule: former major or $500 or more")]["recall"] < lt[("within 5 years", "prior-year giving")]["recall"]),
    ("Lifetime UofU is the largest never-major ratio in the notebook",
     sig("Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "over $5,000", "never_ratio", leak_signals)
     > max(t.filter(pl.col("converters") > 0)["never_ratio"].drop_nulls().max() for t in (signals12, sol_signals, pv_signals, demo_signals))),
]
claim_table = pl.DataFrame({"claim": [c for c, _ in claims], "holds": [bool(ok) for _, ok in claims]})
failed = claim_table.filter(~pl.col("holds"))
assert failed.height == 0, f"claims no longer supported: {failed['claim'].to_list()}"
show(claim_table, caption="Claims in the text checked against the numbers")
```

### Use of AI Tools

All four team members used AI assistants in their individual EDAs, which this notebook draws on. This group notebook was built with Claude Code (Anthropic), which drafted the shared build script (`build_panel.py`), the analysis code, the tables and plots, and first drafts of the prose. The team set every definition and decision, including the fifteen agreed decisions and the later refinements, and each section was reviewed before the next one was written.

AI output was not accepted on trust. It was checked in these ways:

- **Reconciliation.** Every converter count from the four individual EDAs was rebuilt exactly from the shared panel (Reconciling the Four Individual EDAs).
- **Independent checks of the cleaning.** The content-based copy rules were compared with the copy labels in the data, and organization payments were matched to soft credits year by year.
- **Claim checks.** The `{python} n(claim_table.height)` statements in the text that describe a direction or a comparison in words are tested against the numbers in the chunk above, and the render stops if any fails. Several drafted sentences were corrected this way.
- **Reproducibility.** Two consecutive renders produce identical numbers, and the cross-check counts give Samantha's R pipeline a way to confirm the build independently.
- **Reading the output.** Every table, plot, and sentence was read against the rendered numbers before a section was accepted, and wording that overstated a result was revised.

### Team Contributions

This notebook was an even group effort. All four members completed an individual EDA, compared them together, and agreed on the definitions in the decisions table. Each individual EDA contributed the pieces credited in the Purpose section: Erin's clustered bootstrap, lapsed segment, threshold baselines, and legacy history indicators; Benjamin's content-based cleaning rules, snapshot decoding, and FY2026 checks; Kate's master data dictionary and adoption split; and Samantha's time-aware eligibility, response timing rule, and audit trail, along with the R pipeline used as a cross-check.
